### Create `apps/api/test/moderation-intake-order.test.ts`

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import type { SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { PgDialect } from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ModerationError, type ModerationDeps } from "../src/moderation/context";
import { recordIntake, type IntakeGround, type LiveTarget } from "../src/moderation/intake";

/**
 * The order of the intake's transaction (3c design, section 7.1, step 4), without a database: the transaction is a
 * stand-in that records every statement in the order it is issued and answers each as the test scripts it, and the social
 * module is one that records what it is asked to lock and to copy. What the statements do to real rows is in the
 * integration tests; this holds only their order and how often a target's open case is read.
 */

const POST_ONE = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001";
const POST_TWO = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002";
/** An account whose id sorts before both posts': a case's kind comes before its id in the one order. */
const ACCOUNT = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000";
const TAKEN = "2026-10-04T10:00:00.000Z";

const ground: IntakeGround = {
  kind: "user",
  channel: "signed_in",
  reporterId: randomUUID(),
  findingBy: null,
  contactId: null,
  ruleId: "R1",
  allegesIllegal: false,
  csam: false,
  category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  categoryKeyword: null,
  citedLaw: null,
  explanation: null,
  bonaFide: false,
};

/**
 * The module's dependencies over a recording transaction. `openCases` says what each read of a target's open case
 * answers, in order: a case's id, or null for none; when a target's answers run out, its last one is repeated.
 */
function recording(openCases: Record<string, (string | null)[]>) {
  const dialect = new PgDialect();
  const events: string[] = [];
  const reads: Record<string, number> = {};
  let runs = 0;
  const tx = {
    execute: async (query: SQL) => {
      const { sql: text, params } = dialect.sqlToQuery(query);
      const statement = text.trim();
      if (statement.startsWith("select set_config('lock_timeout'")) return [];
      if (statement.startsWith("insert into intakes")) return events.push("intake"), [{ id: randomUUID() }];
      if (statement.startsWith("insert into cases")) return events.push(`open ${String(params[0])} ${String(params[1])}`), [];
      if (statement.startsWith("select id from cases")) {
        const target = String(params[1]);
        const answers = openCases[target] ?? [`case-of-${target}`];
        const answer = answers[Math.min(reads[target] ?? 0, answers.length - 1)];
        reads[target] = (reads[target] ?? 0) + 1;
        events.push(`read ${String(params[0])} ${target}`);
        return answer === null || answer === undefined ? [] : [{ id: answer }];
      }
      if (statement.startsWith("insert into intake_items")) return events.push(`item ${String(params[2])} ${String(params[3])} in ${String(params[1])}`), [{ id: randomUUID(), seq: 1 }];
      if (statement.startsWith("select to_char(")) return events.push("time"), [{ at: TAKEN }];
      if (statement.startsWith("select display_name, bio, handle from evidence_snapshots")) return [];
      if (statement.startsWith("insert into evidence_snapshots")) return events.push(`snapshot ${String(params[1])} ${String(params[2])}`), [{ id: randomUUID(), taken_at: TAKEN }];
      throw new Error(`the intake issued a statement this test does not know: ${statement}`);
    },
  };
  const social = {
    lockAccounts: async () => (events.push("lock sender"), []),
    capturePost: async (_tx: unknown, id: string) => (
      events.push(`copy post ${id}`),
      { id, authorId: randomUUID(), authorHandle: "author", body: "a post", state: "visible", createdAt: new Date(TAKEN), replyToId: null, quoteOfId: null, erased: false }
    ),
    captureProfile: async (_tx: unknown, id: string) => (events.push(`copy account ${id}`), { id, handle: "named", displayName: "Named", bio: "", deleted: false }),
  };
  const apiDb = {
    transaction: async (fn: (transaction: typeof tx) => Promise<unknown>) => {
      runs++;
      events.push(`run ${runs}`);
      return fn(tx);
    },
  };
  const deps = { apiDb, social, config: {}, log: pino({ level: "silent" }), now: () => new Date() } as unknown as ModerationDeps;
  return { deps, events, runs: () => runs };
}

/** The targets in an order that is not the cases' own: the account first, then the later post, then the earlier one. */
const live: LiveTarget[] = [
  { type: "account", id: ACCOUNT, position: 1, namedHandle: "Named" },
  { type: "post", id: POST_TWO, position: 2 },
  { type: "post", id: POST_ONE, position: 3 },
];

describe("the intake's transaction keeps one order", () => {
  test("every case with its item first, posts before accounts and each kind by id, whatever order the request names them in; only then the copies, in that same order", async () => {
    const world = recording({});
    const recorded = await recordIntake(world.deps, { ground, live });
    expect(world.events).toEqual([
      "run 1",
      "lock sender",
      "intake",
      `open post ${POST_ONE}`,
      `read post ${POST_ONE}`,
      `item post ${POST_ONE} in case-of-${POST_ONE}`,
      `open post ${POST_TWO}`,
      `read post ${POST_TWO}`,
      `item post ${POST_TWO} in case-of-${POST_TWO}`,
      `open account ${ACCOUNT}`,
      `read account ${ACCOUNT}`,
      `item account ${ACCOUNT} in case-of-${ACCOUNT}`,
      // No post is copied, and so none is locked, before the last case is taken.
      "time",
      `copy post ${POST_ONE}`,
      `snapshot post ${POST_ONE}`,
      `copy post ${POST_TWO}`,
      `snapshot post ${POST_TWO}`,
      `copy account ${ACCOUNT}`,
      `snapshot account ${ACCOUNT}`,
    ]);
    // The answer lists the items as the request named them.
    expect(recorded.items.map((item) => [item.position, item.targetId])).toEqual([[1, ACCOUNT], [2, POST_TWO], [3, POST_ONE]]);
    // The same request in another order issues the same statements.
    const reversed = recording({});
    await recordIntake(reversed.deps, { ground, live: [...live].reverse() });
    expect(reversed.events).toEqual(world.events);
  });

  test("a target whose open case is read as none twice and found the third time stays in one run: the insert and the read are repeated in the same transaction", async () => {
    const world = recording({ [POST_ONE]: [null, null, "the-new-case"] });
    await recordIntake(world.deps, { ground, live: [{ type: "post", id: POST_ONE, position: 1 }] });
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
    const pair = [`open post ${POST_ONE}`, `read post ${POST_ONE}`];
    expect(world.events).toEqual(["run 1", "lock sender", "intake", ...pair, ...pair, ...pair, `item post ${POST_ONE} in the-new-case`, "time", `copy post ${POST_ONE}`, `snapshot post ${POST_ONE}`]);
  });

  test("three reads that find none start the transaction over, with no item stored without a case; after the fourth run the answer is case_closed", async () => {
    const world = recording({ [POST_TWO]: [null] });
    const err = await recordIntake(world.deps, { ground, live: [{ type: "post", id: POST_ONE, position: 1 }, { type: "post", id: POST_TWO, position: 2 }] }).catch((caught: unknown) => caught);
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(ModerationError);
    expect(err).toMatchObject({ code: "case_closed", status: 409 });
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(4);
    const pair = [`open post ${POST_TWO}`, `read post ${POST_TWO}`];
    const oneRun = (run: number) => [`run ${run}`, "lock sender", "intake", `open post ${POST_ONE}`, `read post ${POST_ONE}`, `item post ${POST_ONE} in case-of-${POST_ONE}`, ...pair, ...pair, ...pair];
    expect(world.events).toEqual([...oneRun(1), ...oneRun(2), ...oneRun(3), ...oneRun(4)]);
    // A target found on a later run is stored then: the third run's reads answer a case.
    const later = recording({ [POST_TWO]: [null, null, null, null, null, null, "a-case-at-last"] });
    const recorded = await recordIntake(later.deps, { ground, live: [{ type: "post", id: POST_TWO, position: 1 }] });
    expect(later.runs()).toBe(3);
    expect(recorded.items.map((item) => item.caseId)).toEqual(["a-case-at-last"]);
  });
});
```

### Create `apps/api/test/moderation-retry.test.ts`

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import type { CaseDecidedParams } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_VERSION, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../src/auth";
import { ModerationError, type ModerationDeps } from "../src/moderation/context";
import { decide } from "../src/moderation/decide";
import { recordIntake, type IntakeGround, type IntakeRecorded } from "../src/moderation/intake";

/**
 * When the moderation module runs a transaction again (3c design, sections 7.1 and 7.5), without a database: the pool is
 * a stand-in whose transaction never runs its statements and ends the way the test scripts it, with the errors PostgreSQL
 * gives and drizzle wraps. The races that produce these errors for real are in the integration tests.
 */

/** PostgreSQL's error as drizzle hands it over: its own error, with the driver's as the cause. */
const pg = (code: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => new Error("Failed query", { cause: Object.assign(new Error(String(extra.message ?? code)), { code, ...extra }) });
const raisedAs = (message: string) => pg("P0001", { message });

/** The module's dependencies over a pool whose transactions end as scripted, one entry for each run; a read finds the case about an account. */
function scripted(ends: (Error | unknown)[], options: { now?: Date; knowsCase?: boolean } = {}) {
  const subject = randomUUID();
  let runs = 0;
  const apiDb = {
    execute: async () => (options.knowsCase === false ? [] : [{ target_type: "account", target_id: subject }]),
    transaction: async () => {
      const end = ends[runs++];
      if (end instanceof Error) throw end;
      if (end === undefined) throw new Error("the transaction ran more often than the test scripted");
      return end;
    },
  };
  const deps = { apiDb, social: {}, config: {}, log: pino({ level: "silent" }), now: () => options.now ?? new Date() } as unknown as ModerationDeps;
  return { deps, runs: () => runs };
}

describe("the intake's transaction is run again when it changed nothing and may now succeed", () => {
  const ground: IntakeGround = {
    kind: "user",
    channel: "signed_in",
    reporterId: randomUUID(),
    findingBy: null,
    contactId: null,
    ruleId: "R1",
    allegesIllegal: false,
    csam: false,
    category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
    categoryKeyword: null,
    citedLaw: null,
    explanation: null,
    bonaFide: false,
  };
  const request = { ground, live: [{ type: "post" as const, id: randomUUID(), position: 1 }] };
  const stored: IntakeRecorded = { intakeId: randomUUID(), ref: "N-ABCDEFGHIJ", token: null, suspect: false, items: [] };

  test("a case that closed under it, a deadlock and a lock timeout each start it over, and the fourth run's answer is the intake's", async () => {
    // The attach trigger reports a closed case as a serialization failure.
    const world = scripted([pg("40001", { message: "case_closed" }), pg("40P01"), pg("55P03"), stored]);
    expect(await recordIntake(world.deps, request)).toBe(stored);
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(4);
  });

  test("a reference another intake already has starts it over too: the next run draws a new one", async () => {
    const world = scripted([pg("23505", { constraint_name: "intakes_ref_unique" }), stored]);
    expect(await recordIntake(world.deps, request)).toBe(stored);
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(2);
  });

  test("when the fourth run fails the same way the answer is case_closed, and no fifth run is made", async () => {
    const world = scripted([pg("40001"), pg("40001"), pg("40P01"), pg("55P03")]);
    await expect(recordIntake(world.deps, request)).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "ModerationError", code: "case_closed", status: 409 });
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(4);
  });

  test("a second report by the same sender on the same ground is already_reported, at once", async () => {
    const world = scripted([pg("23505", { constraint_name: "intake_items_reporter_once" })]);
    await expect(recordIntake(world.deps, request)).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "ModerationError", code: "already_reported" });
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
  });

  test("any other error is thrown as it is, at once", async () => {
    for (const failure of [pg("23503"), pg("23505", { constraint_name: "intake_items_target_once" }), pg("P0001", { message: "quote_item_missing" }), new Error("the connection ended")]) {
      const world = scripted([failure]);
      await expect(recordIntake(world.deps, request)).rejects.toBe(failure);
      expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
    }
  });
});

describe("a confirmed decision's transaction is run once more only when it changed nothing and time is left", () => {
  const caseId = randomUUID();
  const keyId = randomUUID();
  const session = { userId: randomUUID(), keyId, handle: randomUUID(), role: "admin" } as unknown as ActiveStaffSession;
  const params: CaseDecidedParams = {
    kind: "final",
    stateVersion: 0,
    throughSeq: 1,
    reviewsDecisionId: null,
    snapshotId: randomUUID(),
    snapshotDigest: "a".repeat(64),
    outcome: "no_violation",
    ground: null,
    ruleId: null,
    rulesVersion: RULES_VERSION,
    redressVersion: REDRESS_VERSION,
    category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
    categoryKeyword: null,
    actions: [],
    factsDigest: null,
    reasonDigest: null,
    legalReferenceDigest: null,
  };
  const now = new Date("2026-10-04T12:00:00.000Z");
  /** A confirmation of the params whose challenge has this many seconds left. */
  const confirmed = (secondsLeft: number, changed: Partial<CaseDecidedParams> = {}): StaffStepUpConfirmed => ({
    action: "case_decided",
    target: { type: "case", id: caseId },
    params: { ...params, ...changed },
    actionHash: "b".repeat(64),
    keyId,
    assertion: { authenticatorData: "AAAA", clientDataJSON: "BBBB", signature: "CCCC" },
    expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + secondsLeft * 1000),
  });
  const run = (world: ReturnType<typeof scripted>, secondsLeft = 600, changed: Partial<CaseDecidedParams> = {}) => decide(world.deps, session, confirmed(secondsLeft, changed), { requestId: "req-1" });
  const done = { decisionId: randomUUID() };

  test("a deadlock or a lock timeout runs it once more with the same confirmation", async () => {
    for (const code of ["40P01", "55P03"]) {
      const world = scripted([pg(code), done], { now });
      expect(await run(world), code).toBe(done);
      expect(world.runs(), code).toBe(2);
    }
  });

  test("a second failure of that kind is answered as late, without a third run", async () => {
    const world = scripted([pg("40P01"), pg("55P03")], { now });
    expect(await run(world)).toBe("late");
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(2);
  });

  test("with a minute or less of the challenge left it is not run again", async () => {
    for (const secondsLeft of [60, 5]) {
      const world = scripted([pg("40P01")], { now });
      expect(await run(world, secondsLeft), String(secondsLeft)).toBe("late");
      expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
    }
    const world = scripted([pg("40P01"), done], { now });
    expect(await run(world, 61)).toBe(done);
  });

  test("the audit row's refusals are answers, not errors: the key or the account ended, or the challenge's time ran out", async () => {
    expect(await run(scripted([raisedAs("staff_confirmation_ended")], { now }))).toBe("ended");
    expect(await run(scripted([raisedAs("staff_confirmation_late")], { now }))).toBe("late");
  });

  test("a code a trigger raised is thrown as its ModerationError; anything else as it is", async () => {
    for (const code of ["case_changed", "staff_recused", "staff_target", "admin_required", "decision_cap", "profile_changed", "snapshot_mismatch", "snapshot_erased", "text_not_found", "invalid_decision"] as const) {
      const world = scripted([raisedAs(code)], { now });
      await expect(run(world), code).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "ModerationError", code });
      expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
    }
    for (const failure of [raisedAs("something_else"), pg("23503"), pg("40001")]) {
      const world = scripted([failure], { now });
      await expect(run(world)).rejects.toBe(failure);
      expect(world.runs()).toBe(1);
    }
  });

  test("a decision under other texts than the API serves is refused before anything is read or written", async () => {
    for (const changed of [{ redressVersion: REDRESS_VERSION + 1 }, { rulesVersion: RULES_VERSION - 1 }]) {
      const world = scripted([done], { now });
      await expect(run(world, 600, changed)).rejects.toMatchObject({ name: "ModerationError", code: "invalid_decision" });
      expect(world.runs()).toBe(0);
    }
  });

  test("a case that does not exist is not found", async () => {
    const world = scripted([done], { now, knowsCase: false });
    const err = await run(world).catch((caught: unknown) => caught);
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(ModerationError);
    expect(err).toMatchObject({ code: "not_found", status: 404 });
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(0);
  });

  test("a confirmation of anything but this decision by this session's key is a wiring fault, not a refusal", async () => {
    const world = scripted([done], { now });
    const other = { ...confirmed(600), keyId: randomUUID() };
    await expect(decide(world.deps, session, other, { requestId: "req-1" })).rejects.toThrow(/needs a step-up that confirmed it/);
    const revoked = { ...confirmed(600), action: "staff_session_revoked" } as unknown as StaffStepUpConfirmed;
    await expect(decide(world.deps, session, revoked, { requestId: "req-1" })).rejects.toThrow(/needs a step-up that confirmed it/);
    expect(world.runs()).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/architecture.test.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, posix, relative, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

/**
 * Module boundaries (1a spec section 2.2, 2a spec section 2.2, 3a design section 5, 3c design section 5). Paths are relative to apps/api/src
 * with forward slashes. The rules are plain functions so the tests below can prove each one catches
 * a deliberate violation.
 */
interface SourceFile {
  path: string;
  source: string;
}

const SRC_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../src", import.meta.url));
const SCHEMA_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../packages/db/src/schema", import.meta.url));

/** Schema files that define auth-schema objects or shared helpers; every other schema file is public. */
const NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES = new Set(["auth.ts", "helpers.ts", "index.ts"]);
const AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE = "auth.ts";
// The command lines open both pools: grant-role changes a role on the auth pool, and staff.js reads there the staff keys
// that audit-verify checks the record against.
const AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts", "index.ts", "cli/grant-role.ts", "cli/staff.ts"]);
const AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts"]);

/** Modules that may only be entered through their index file. */
const MODULES = ["auth", "social", "media", "account", "staff", "moderation"] as const;

function walk(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return walk(full);
    return entry.name.endsWith(".ts") ? [full] : [];
  });
}

function loadSources(): SourceFile[] {
  return walk(SRC_ROOT).map((full) => ({ path: relative(SRC_ROOT, full).split(sep).join("/"), source: readFileSync(full, "utf8") }));
}

function exportedNames(file: string): string[] {
  const source = readFileSync(join(SCHEMA_ROOT, file), "utf8");
  return [...source.matchAll(/^export (?:const|function|type|interface|enum) ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Names exported by the public-schema files of @korbat/db (tables and enums the auth module must not touch). */
function publicSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  for (const file of readdirSync(SCHEMA_ROOT)) {
    if (!file.endsWith(".ts") || NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES.has(file)) continue;
    for (const name of exportedNames(file)) names.add(name);
  }
  return names;
}

/** Names exported by the auth-schema file of @korbat/db (tables and enums the social module must not touch). */
function authSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  return new Set(exportedNames(AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE));
}

/** Every module specifier in static imports, re-exports, side-effect imports and dynamic imports. */
function specifiers(source: string): string[] {
  return [...source.matchAll(/(?:\bfrom\s+|\bimport\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s+)["']([^"']+)["']/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Named bindings of every `import { ... } from "@korbat/db"`; a namespace import yields the marker "*". */
function dbImports(source: string): string[] {
  const names: string[] = [];
  for (const match of source.matchAll(/\bimport\s+(type\s+)?(\*\s+as\s+\w+|\{[^}]*\})\s+from\s+["'](@korbat\/db(?:\/[^"']*)?)["']/g)) {
    const bindings = match[2]!;
    if (bindings.startsWith("*")) {
      names.push("*");
      continue;
    }
    for (const part of bindings.slice(1, -1).split(",")) {
      const name = part.trim().replace(/^type\s+/, "").split(/\s+as\s+/)[0]!.trim();
      if (name) names.push(name);
    }
  }
  return names;
}

const insideAuth = (path: string) => path.startsWith("auth/");
const insideSocial = (path: string) => path.startsWith("social/");
const insideMedia = (path: string) => path.startsWith("media/");
const insideAccount = (path: string) => path.startsWith("account/");
const insideStaff = (path: string) => path.startsWith("staff/");
const insideModeration = (path: string) => path.startsWith("moderation/");

function findViolations(files: SourceFile[], publicNames: Set<string>, authNames: Set<string>): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/\.ts$/, "");
      for (const module of MODULES) {
        if (path.startsWith(`${module}/`)) continue;
        if (target.startsWith(`${module}/`) && target !== `${module}/index`) {
          violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is inside the ${module} module (use ./${module})`);
        }
      }
    }
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(DATABASE_URL_AUTH|authDb)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references the auth database pool`);
    }
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(TOTP_ENC_KEY|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|IP_HASH_KEY)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references an auth key`);
    }
    if (insideAuth(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import auth-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    if (!insideMedia(path) && /\b(postMedia|post_media)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references post_media, which only the media module may touch`);
    }
    // The staff module (role korbat_api) reads and writes the public audit log; staff keys, staff sessions and enrolments
    // are credentials, the auth module's alone (3a design, section 5). The moderation module owns the moderation tables on
    // the same role: a notifier's contact and the staff links live in the auth schema, out of its reach (3c design, section 5).
    if (insideSocial(path) || insideMedia(path) || insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import public-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    // The account module sequences the other three through their index files and holds no table access of its own
    // (1b spec, section 5): no table or enum of either schema may be named in it. Db and DbTx, which are not schema
    // names, stay allowed, since a transaction is passed through it.
    if (insideAccount(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
      }
    }
    // The staff module uses the auth module's interface as the other modules do, never its repository or its session
    // store, which would hand it the auth tables; the moderation module likewise. Any mention counts, so a renamed,
    // namespace or dynamic import is caught as surely as a named one.
    if (insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      const module = insideStaff(path) ? "staff" : "moderation";
      for (const name of new Set([...source.matchAll(/\b(createAuthRepo|createSessions)\b/g)].map((m) => m[1]!))) {
        violations.push(`${path}: uses the auth module's ${name} (the ${module} module goes through the auth module's interface)`);
      }
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("module boundaries", () => {
  test("walks the real source tree", () => {
    const paths = loadSources().map((f) => f.path);
    expect(paths).toContain("auth/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("social/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("media/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("account/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("staff/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("moderation/index.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("cli/staff.ts");
    expect(paths).toContain("app.ts");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).toContain("profiles");
    expect(publicSchemaNames()).not.toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).toContain("users");
    expect(authSchemaNames()).not.toContain("posts");
  });

  test("apps/api/src has no boundary violations", () => {
    expect(findViolations(loadSources(), publicSchemaNames(), authSchemaNames())).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("allows the module indexes, the permitted pool owners and each module's own schema", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createAuth } from "./auth";\nimport type { Auth } from "./auth/index";\nimport { createSocial } from "./social";` },
      { path: "profiles/store.ts", source: `import { isUniqueViolation } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "cli/grant-role.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "config.ts", source: `AUTH_HMAC_KEY: base64Key, IP_HASH_KEY: base64Key, TOTP_ENC_KEY: versionedKey, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: url` },
      { path: "auth/repo.ts", source: `import { users, sessions, type Db } from "@korbat/db";\nconst k = config.TOTP_ENC_KEY;` },
      { path: "social/repo.ts", source: `import { posts, profiles, type Db } from "@korbat/db";\nimport { SocialError } from "./context";` },
      { path: "social/routes.ts", source: `import type { Auth } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `import { createAccount } from "./account";\nimport { createMedia } from "./media";` },
      { path: "account/routes.ts", source: `import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";\nimport type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";\nimport { buildExport } from "./flows/export";` },
      { path: "account/flows/deletion.ts", source: `import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";\nimport type { MediaForAccount } from "../../media";` },
      { path: "cli/staff.ts", source: `import { createStaff } from "../staff";\nconst authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `import { auditHead, auditLog, profiles, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "staff/routes.ts", source: `import { AuthError, type Auth } from "../auth";\nimport { staffGate } from "./gate";` },
      { path: "staff/cases.ts", source: `import { ModerationError, type ModerationForStaff } from "../moderation";` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `import { createModeration } from "./moderation";\nimport { socialForModeration } from "./social";` },
      { path: "moderation/repo.ts", source: `import { cases, decisions, evidenceSnapshots, intakes, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";\nimport { ModerationError } from "./context";` },
      { path: "moderation/decide.ts", source: `import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";\nimport { boundLockWaits } from "../lib/lock-bounds";\nimport type { SocialForModeration } from "../social";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["profiles", "posts", "auditLog", "auditHead", "cases", "decisions", "evidenceSnapshots", "intakes"]), new Set(["users", "sessions"]))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the auth module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "routes/posts.ts", source: `import { hashPassword } from "../auth/passwords";` },
      { path: "app.ts", source: `export { createSessions } from "./auth/sessions.ts";\nconst m = await import("./auth/repo");` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "routes/posts.ts: imports ../auth/passwords, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
      "app.ts: imports ./auth/sessions.ts, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
      "app.ts: imports ./auth/repo, which is inside the auth module (use ./auth)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the social module, from outside it and from the auth module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createSocialRepo } from "./social/repo";` },
      { path: "auth/flows/signup.ts", source: `import { createPost } from "../../social/flows/posts";` },
      { path: "social/flows/graph.ts", source: `import { ownProfile } from "./posts";` },

    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./social/repo, which is inside the social module (use ./social)",
      "auth/flows/signup.ts: imports ../../social/flows/posts, which is inside the social module (use ./social)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the media module, post_media outside it, and the auth schema inside it", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createMediaRepo } from "./media/repo";\nimport { createMedia } from "./media";` },
      { path: "social/repo.ts", source: `import { postMedia, posts } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const rows = await db.execute(sql`select * from post_media`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: `import { postMedia, posts, users, type Db } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "media/flows/serve.ts", source: `import type { MediaDeps } from "../context";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["posts", "postMedia"]), new Set(["users"]))).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./media/repo, which is inside the media module (use ./media)",
      "social/repo.ts: references post_media, which only the media module may touch",
      "social/views.ts: references post_media, which only the media module may touch",
      "media/repo.ts: imports auth-schema users from @korbat/db",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the account module, and a table or enum of either schema inside it", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { createZipWriter } from "./account/zip";\nimport { createAccount } from "./account";` },
      { path: "social/flows/graph.ts", source: `import { buildExport } from "../../account/flows/export";` },
      { path: "account/flows/export.ts", source: `import { posts, users, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "account/purge.ts", source: `import * as db from "@korbat/db";` },

    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["posts"]), new Set(["users"]))).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./account/zip, which is inside the account module (use ./account)",
      "social/flows/graph.ts: imports ../../account/flows/export, which is inside the account module (use ./account)",
      "account/flows/export.ts: imports public-schema posts from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
      "account/flows/export.ts: imports auth-schema users from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
      "account/purge.ts: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches auth pool and auth key references outside their owners", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "routes/posts.ts", source: `const url = config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH;` },
      { path: "profiles/store.ts", source: `export function f(authDb: Db) {}` },
      { path: "lib/hash.ts", source: `const key = config.IP_HASH_KEY;` },
      { path: "index.ts", source: `const k = config.AUTH_HMAC_KEY;` },
      // The staff command line may open the auth pool; another command line, or the staff module itself, may not.
      { path: "cli/other.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `export function readKeys(authDb: Db) {}` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "routes/posts.ts: references the auth database pool",
      "profiles/store.ts: references the auth database pool",
      "lib/hash.ts: references an auth key",
      "index.ts: references an auth key",
      "cli/other.ts: references the auth database pool",
      "staff/audit.ts: references the auth database pool",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a deep import into the staff module, from outside it and from the auth module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "app.ts", source: `import { staffGate } from "./staff/gate";\nimport { createStaff } from "./staff";` },
      { path: "cli/staff.ts", source: `import { canonicalText } from "../staff/chain";` },
      { path: "auth/staff/flows.ts", source: `import { appendAuditRow } from "../../staff/audit";` },
      { path: "staff/routes.ts", source: `import { staffGate } from "./gate";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "app.ts: imports ./staff/gate, which is inside the staff module (use ./staff)",
      "cli/staff.ts: imports ../staff/chain, which is inside the staff module (use ./staff)",
      "auth/staff/flows.ts: imports ../../staff/audit, which is inside the staff module (use ./staff)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches auth-schema imports inside the staff module", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `import { auditLog, staffKeys, type Db } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "staff/reader.ts", source: `import type { staffSessions as s } from "@korbat/db";` },
      { path: "staff/writer.ts", source: `import * as db from "@korbat/db";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(["auditLog"]), new Set(["staffKeys", "staffSessions"]))).toEqual([
      "staff/audit.ts: imports auth-schema staffKeys from @korbat/db",
      "staff/reader.ts: imports auth-schema staffSessions from @korbat/db",
      "staff/writer.ts: namespace import of @korbat/db (import public-schema names explicitly)",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches the auth module's repository or session store inside the staff module, however it is imported", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `import { AuthError, createAuthRepo } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "staff/routes.ts", source: `import { createSessions as sessionsOf } from "../auth";` },
      { path: "staff/flows/x.ts", source: `import * as auth from "../../auth";\nconst repo = auth.createAuthRepo(db);\nconst s = auth.createSessions(deps);` },
      { path: "staff/flows/y.ts", source: `const { createSessions } = await import("../../auth");` },
      // Outside the staff module the rule does not apply: the command lines build the auth module's parts themselves.
      { path: "cli/grant-role.ts", source: `import { createAuthRepo, createSessions } from "../auth";` },
    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([
      "staff/audit.ts: uses the auth module's createAuthRepo (the staff module goes through the auth module's interface)",
      "staff/routes.ts: uses the auth module's createSessions (the staff module goes through the auth module's interface)",
      "staff/flows/x.ts: uses the auth module's createAuthRepo (the staff module goes through the auth module's interface)",
      "staff/flows/x.ts: uses the auth module's createSessions (the staff module goes through the auth module's interface)",
      "staff/flows/y.ts: uses the auth module's createSessions (the staff module goes through the auth module's interface)",
    ]);

  test("catches a deep import into the moderation module, from outside it and from another module", () => {
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { and, eq, gt, inArray, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { stepUpActionHash } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { auditHead, auditLog, closeDb, createDb, staffKeys, users, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { createAuthRepo, type AuthRepo } from "../../src/auth/repo";
import { AUDIT_VERIFY_PAGE_SIZE, auditVerify, checkAuditRecord, runStaffCommand, type AuditReport } from "../../src/cli/staff";
import { loadConfig } from "../../src/config";
import { SoftAuthenticator } from "../auth/soft-authenticator";
import { CHAIN_VECTORS } from "../staff/chain-vectors";
import { flowHarness } from "./flow-harness";
import { enrolKey } from "./staff-enrolment";
import { TEST_CONSOLE, TEST_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, issueEnrolment, newStaffAccount, newStaffKey, rolledBack, withLockTimeout } from "./staff-fixtures";
import { revokeConfirmed, signedIn } from "./staff-step-up";

/**
 * audit-verify (3a design, sections 7 and 12) against the real database: the canonical text in Node against the trigger's
 * in SQL, the chain under concurrent writers, rewrites by the owner detected against kept places, and every staff key's
 * one staff_key_added row. Every test that writes a row audit-verify must refuse does it in a transaction that ends in a
 * rollback and hands that transaction to the verifier's check, so no later suite sees a broken chain.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: audit-verify", () => {
  let apiDb: Db;
  let authDb: Db;
  let migrateDb: Db;
  let repo: AuthRepo;
  const actorId = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000";

  /** One ordinary row, as a writer on the API role inserts it: no id, time or chain column supplied. */
  const insertRow = (db: Db | DbTx, action = `probe-${randomUUID()}`) =>
    db.insert(auditLog).values({ actorId, action, targetType: "user", targetId: randomUUID(), metadata: { via: "test" } }).returning();

  const readHead = async (db: Db | DbTx = apiDb) => (await db.select().from(auditHead))[0]!;
  const hashAt = async (seq: number) => (await apiDb.select({ hash: auditLog.hash }).from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, seq)))[0]!.hash;

  /**
   * What the owner can do: chain every row from place `from` again with the database's own text function, as migration
   * 0012's back-fill does, and move the head, so a plain recompute of the chain passes over the changed rows.
   */
  const rechainFrom = (tx: DbTx, from: number) =>
    tx.execute(
      sql.raw(`DO $$
        DECLARE r public.audit_log; prev text;
        BEGIN
          SELECT hash INTO prev FROM public.audit_log WHERE chain_seq = ${from - 1};
          FOR r IN SELECT * FROM public.audit_log WHERE chain_seq >= ${from} ORDER BY chain_seq LOOP
            prev := encode(sha256(convert_to(prev || public.audit_chain_text(r), 'UTF8')), 'hex');
            UPDATE public.audit_log SET prev_hash = (SELECT hash FROM public.audit_log WHERE chain_seq = r.chain_seq - 1), hash = prev WHERE id = r.id;
          END LOOP;
          UPDATE public.audit_head SET hash = prev WHERE id = 1;
        END $$`),
    );

  /** The verifier's own connections, as the command line opens them: one on each role. */
  const ownConnections = () => ({ api: createDb(loadConfig().DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 1 }), auth: createDb(loadConfig().DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 1 }) });

  /**
   * What the command line printed, and its exit code, for a run with the given environment changes; with `inherit` false,
   * the run sees `env` alone and nothing of the test environment.
   */
  async function cli(args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}, inherit = true) {
    const lines: string[] = [];
    const code = await runStaffCommand(args, inherit ? { ...process.env, ...env } : env, { log: (line) => lines.push(line), error: (line) => lines.push(line) });
    return { code, text: lines.join("\n") };
  }

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const config = loadConfig();
    apiDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 4 });
    authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 4 });
    // The migrate role is not part of the API configuration; the test environment carries it.
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 2 });
    repo = createAuthRepo(authDb);
    // A few committed rows, so the log is never empty whatever order the suites run in.
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) await withLockTimeout(apiDb, (tx) => insertRow(tx));
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await Promise.all([closeDb(apiDb), closeDb(authDb), closeDb(migrateDb)]);
  });

  test("a whole chain passes, with the head, and every kept place it is given", async () => {
    const head = await readHead();
    const connections = ownConnections();
    try {
      const plain = await auditVerify(connections, []);
      expect(plain).toMatchObject({ ok: true, rows: head.seq, head: { seq: head.seq, hash: head.hash }, keptChecked: 0, unanchored: head.seq, problems: [], problemCount: 0 });
      const kept = await auditVerify(connections, [
        { seq: 1, hash: await hashAt(1) },
        { seq: head.seq - 1, hash: await hashAt(head.seq - 1) },
      ]);
      expect(kept).toMatchObject({ ok: true, keptChecked: 2, unanchored: 1, problems: [] });
    } finally {
      await Promise.all([closeDb(connections.api), closeDb(connections.auth)]);
    }
  });

  describe("parity: the canonical text in Node and in SQL", () => {
    test("the vectors' rows, written through the trigger from a session in another time zone and date style, recompute to their stored hashes", async () => {
      // One connection, so the session's settings hold for the transaction below.
      const odd = createDb(loadConfig().DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 1 });
      try {
        await odd.execute(sql`set timezone = 'Asia/Kathmandu'`);
        await odd.execute(sql`set datestyle = 'SQL, DMY'`);
        // Rolled back: the step-up row carries an assertion no stored key made, which audit-verify's step-up checks refuse.
        await rolledBack(odd, async (tx) => {
          const [settings] = await tx.execute<{ tz: string; ds: string }>(sql`select current_setting('TimeZone') as tz, current_setting('DateStyle') as ds`);
          expect(settings).toEqual({ tz: "Asia/Kathmandu", ds: "SQL, DMY" });
          const before = await readHead(tx);
          const written: number[] = [];
          for (const vector of CHAIN_VECTORS) {
            const [row] = await tx.insert(auditLog).values(vector.insert).returning({ id: auditLog.id });
            written.push(row!.id);
          }
          // The stored jsonb prints as the vectors say, so the unit vectors hold chain.ts to what the database embeds.
          const texts = await tx
            .select({ id: auditLog.id, metadata: sql<string>`${auditLog.metadata}::text`, stepUp: sql<string | null>`${auditLog.stepUp}::text` })
            .from(auditLog)
            .where(inArray(auditLog.id, written))
            .orderBy(auditLog.chainSeq);
          expect(texts.map((t) => [t.metadata, t.stepUp])).toEqual(CHAIN_VECTORS.map((v) => [v.metadataText, v.stepUpText]));

          // The API role cannot read the staff keys: they come from the auth role's pool, as the command line reads them.
          // Every hash recomputes. Two rows are refused for what they are: the step-up vector, whose assertion no stored
          // key made, and which is the last vector; and the vector that records a decision on a case with no step-up at
          // all, an action that only a staff key's confirmation may leave in the record.
          const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, [], authDb);
          expect(CHAIN_VECTORS.at(-1)!.insert.stepUp).not.toBeNull();
          expect(CHAIN_VECTORS.filter((vector) => vector.insert.stepUp !== null)).toHaveLength(1);
          const unconfirmed = CHAIN_VECTORS.findIndex((vector) => vector.insert.action === "case_decided" && vector.insert.stepUp === null);
          expect(unconfirmed).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
          expect(report.problems).toEqual([
            { place: before.seq + unconfirmed + 1, message: "its action, case_decided, needs a step-up, and it carries none" },
            { place: before.seq + CHAIN_VECTORS.length, message: expect.stringMatching(/^its step-up/) },
          ]);
          expect(report.rows).toBe(before.seq + CHAIN_VECTORS.length);
        });
      } finally {
        await closeDb(odd);
      }
    });
  });

  describe("concurrency", () => {
    test("several sessions insert at once, some inside transactions, while keys are enrolled: every run passes, during and after", async () => {
      const WRITERS = 6;
      const EACH = 10;
      const config = loadConfig();
      // One connection per writer, each with a lock timeout for the whole session.
      const writers = Array.from({ length: WRITERS }, () => createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 1 }));
      const connections = ownConnections();
      const reports: AuditReport[] = [];
      let writing = true;
      try {
        await Promise.all(writers.map((db) => db.execute(sql`set lock_timeout = '10s'`)));
        const verifying = (async () => {
          while (writing) reports.push(await auditVerify(connections, []));
        })();
        await Promise.all([
          ...writers.map(async (db, w) => {
            for (let i = 0; i < EACH; i++) {
              const action = `concurrent-verify-${w}-${i}`;
              if (i % 2 === 0) {
                await insertRow(db, action);
              } else {
                // A transaction that waits a moment before its insert, which is its last statement, as every audit write's.
                await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
                  await tx.execute(sql`select pg_sleep(${Math.random() * 0.01})`);
                  await insertRow(tx, action);
                });
              }
            }
          }),
          // Keys enrolled meanwhile: a key whose staff_key_added row lies beyond the head a run read is left to the next run.
          (async () => {
            for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);

        await verifying;

        const head = await readHead();

        expect(reports.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        for (const report of reports) expect(report.problems).toEqual([]);
        expect(final).toMatchObject({ ok: true, rows: head.seq, head: { seq: head.seq, hash: head.hash }, keysLeftToNextRun: 0, problems: [] });
        expect(final.keysChecked).toBe(await migrateDb.$count(staffKeys));
      } finally {
        writing = false;
        await Promise.all([...writers.map((db) => closeDb(db)), closeDb(connections.api), closeDb(connections.auth)]);
      }
    });
  });

  describe("rewrites by the owner", () => {
    test("a row changed alone fails a plain run, naming its place", async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [row] = await insertRow(tx, "rewrite-alone");
        await insertRow(tx, "rewrite-alone-after");
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ metadata: { via: "edited" } }).where(eq(auditLog.id, row!.id));
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.ok).toBe(false);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([{ place: row!.chainSeq, message: "its hash does not match its content" }]);
      });

        expect((await auditVerify(connections, [])).ok).toBe(true);
      } finally {

      }
    });

    test("a row changed with every later hash and the head recomputed passes a plain run, and fails against a place kept before the change", async () => {
      const head = await readHead();
      const target = head.seq - 1;
      const keptBefore = { seq: target - 1, hash: await hashAt(target - 1) };
      const keptAfter = { seq: head.seq, hash: head.hash };
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ action: "rewritten" }).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, target));
        await rechainFrom(tx, target);
        expect((await readHead(tx)).hash).not.toBe(head.hash);

        const plain = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(plain.problems).toEqual([]);
        // A place kept before the changed row still holds; the one kept at or after it no longer does.
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [keptBefore])).problems).toEqual([]);
        const anchored = await checkAuditRecord(tx, [keptBefore, keptAfter]);
        expect(anchored.ok).toBe(false);

      });
    });
  });

  describe("rewrites by the owner that each check of the chain catches", () => {
    /** Three new rows, as a writer inserts them, in the transaction `tx`; the newest is the head. */
    const threeRows = async (tx: DbTx) => {
      const first = (await insertRow(tx, "probe-a"))[0]!;
      const middle = (await insertRow(tx, "probe-b"))[0]!;
      const last = (await insertRow(tx, "probe-c"))[0]!;
      return [first, middle, last] as const;
    };

    test("a row changed with only its own hash recomputed breaks its link to the next row, which a later kept place does not see", async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {

        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ metadata: { via: "edited" } }).where(eq(auditLog.id, middle.id));
        // The owner recomputes the changed row's own hash over its stored prev_hash, with the database's own text.
        await tx.execute(sql`update public.audit_log a set hash = encode(sha256(convert_to(a.prev_hash || public.audit_chain_text(a), 'UTF8')), 'hex') where a.id = ${middle.id}`);

      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {

        await tx.delete(auditLog).where(gt(auditLog.chainSeq, first.chainSeq));
        await tx.update(auditHead).set({ seq: first.chainSeq, hash: first.hash }).where(eq(auditHead.id, 1));
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [])).problems).toEqual([]);
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [kept])).problems).toEqual([{ place: kept.seq, message: `the kept place ${kept.seq}:${kept.hash} no longer matches: no row is at that place` }]);
      });
    });

    test("the head: missing, behind the newest row, beyond it, or with another hash", async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.delete(auditHead);
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [])).problems).toEqual([{ place: null, message: "the audit head is missing" }]);
      });
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [first, middle] = await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.update(auditHead).set({ seq: first.chainSeq, hash: first.hash }).where(eq(auditHead.id, 1));
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [])).problems).toEqual([{ place: middle.chainSeq, message: `rows lie beyond the head's place ${first.chainSeq}, from place ${middle.chainSeq}` }]);
      });
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [, , last] = await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.update(auditHead).set({ seq: last.chainSeq + 5 }).where(eq(auditHead.id, 1));
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [])).problems).toEqual([{ place: null, message: `the head names place ${last.chainSeq + 5}, but the newest row up to it is at place ${last.chainSeq}` }]);
      });
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [, , last] = await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.update(auditHead).set({ hash: "e".repeat(64) }).where(eq(auditHead.id, 1));
        expect((await checkAuditRecord(tx, [])).problems).toEqual([{ place: last.chainSeq, message: "the head's hash is not the hash of the row at its place" }]);
      });
    });

    test("a row moved to place 0, or beyond the head, is named", async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [, middle] = await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ chainSeq: 0 }).where(eq(auditLog.id, middle.id));
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: 0, message: "its place is not in the chain, which runs from place 1" });
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: middle.chainSeq, message: `place ${middle.chainSeq} is missing` });
      });
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const [, middle, last] = await threeRows(tx);
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ chainSeq: last.chainSeq + 10 }).where(eq(auditLog.id, middle.id));
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: last.chainSeq + 10, message: `rows lie beyond the head's place ${last.chainSeq}, from place ${last.chainSeq + 10}` });
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: middle.chainSeq, message: `place ${middle.chainSeq} is missing` });
      });
    });

    /**
     * What the owner can do to plant a row the walk by place never reaches: turn the trigger off and drop the unique index
     * on chain_seq (or its NOT NULL), then insert. The planted row is a step-up action's with no confirmation, which a walk
     * that read it would refuse; it repeats the genuine row's prev_hash and hash, so no other row or the head changes.
     */
    const plant = (tx: DbTx, place: number | null, copy: { prevHash: string; hash: string }) =>
      tx.execute(sql`insert into public.audit_log (actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, metadata, chain_version, chain_seq, prev_hash, hash)
        values (${actorId}::uuid, 'staff_session_revoked', 'staff_session', ${randomUUID()}, '{"params": {}}'::jsonb, 1, ${place}::bigint, ${copy.prevHash}, ${copy.hash})`);

    test("a second row at a place that ends a page of the walk is read and refused", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        // Enough rows that a page of the walk ends at a place, with rows after it.
        const page = AUDIT_VERIFY_PAGE_SIZE;
        const short = page + 5 - (await readHead(tx)).seq;
        if (short > 0) {
          await tx.execute(sql`insert into public.audit_log (actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, metadata)
            select ${actorId}::uuid, 'probe-page', 'user', gen_random_uuid()::text, '{"via": "test"}'::jsonb from generate_series(1, ${short})`);
        }
        const [genuine] = await tx.select().from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, page));
        await tx.execute(sql`alter table public.audit_log disable trigger audit_chain`);
        await tx.execute(sql`drop index public.audit_log_chain_seq_idx`);
        // A plain index in its place, as the owner might leave it: equal places come back oldest row first, so a walk by
        // place alone reads the genuine row and never the second.
        await tx.execute(sql`create index audit_log_chain_seq_plain on public.audit_log (chain_seq)`);
        await plant(tx, page, genuine!);
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.ok).toBe(false);
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: page, message: "another row is already at this place" });
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: page, message: "its action, staff_session_revoked, needs a step-up, and it carries none" });
        expect(report.problems).toContainEqual({ place: null, message: "1 row is at a place another row already holds" });
      });
    });

    test("a row with no place at all is counted and refused", { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const head = await readHead(tx);
        const [newest] = await tx.select().from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, head.seq));
        await tx.execute(sql`alter table public.audit_log disable trigger audit_chain`);
        await tx.execute(sql`alter table public.audit_log alter column chain_seq drop not null`);
        await plant(tx, null, newest!);
        const total = (await tx.select({ n: sql<string>`count(*)::text` }).from(auditLog))[0]!.n;
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.ok).toBe(false);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([
          { place: null, message: "1 row of the audit log has no place in the chain" },
          { place: null, message: `the audit log holds ${total} rows, but ${head.seq} were read up to the head and 0 lie beyond it` },
        ]);
      });
    });
  });

  describe("step-up confirmations", () => {
    const harness = () => flowHarness(repo, { console: TEST_CONSOLE });

    /**
     * A staff account with a key enrolled through the flow and three sessions; from the first it revokes the other two,
     * each confirmed with the key through the step-up flow: two genuine step-up rows, committed, as only the flow writes them.
     */
    async function confirmedRevocations() {
      const h = harness();
      const { user } = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      const soft = new SoftAuthenticator();
      const enrolled = await enrolKey(h, soft, (await issueEnrolment(migrateDb, user.id)).token);
      const [a, b, c] = [await signedIn(h, soft, enrolled.credentialId, 1), await signedIn(h, soft, enrolled.credentialId, 2), await signedIn(h, soft, enrolled.credentialId, 3)];
      expect((await revokeConfirmed(h, soft, enrolled.credentialId, a.session, b.session.handle, 4)).revoked).toBe(true);
      expect((await revokeConfirmed(h, soft, enrolled.credentialId, a.session, c.session.handle, 5)).revoked).toBe(true);
      const rowOf = async (handle: string) => (await apiDb.select().from(auditLog).where(and(eq(auditLog.action, "staff_session_revoked"), eq(auditLog.targetId, handle))))[0]!;
      return { user, keyId: enrolled.key.id, a: a.session, b: b.session, c: c.session, first: await rowOf(b.session.handle), second: await rowOf(c.session.handle) };
    }

    /** The problems a check found, as place and message, each expected to name the step-up check. */
    const stepUpProblems = (report: AuditReport) => report.problems.map((p) => ({ place: p.place, stepUp: /step-up/.test(p.message) }));

    test("genuine confirmations pass: on the command line's own connections, with the console off, and with nothing but the database URLs", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      expect(s.first).toMatchObject({ staffSession: s.a.handle, keyId: s.keyId, actorId: s.user.id });
      expect(s.first.stepUp).not.toBeNull();
      const connections = ownConnections();
      try {
        const report = await auditVerify(connections, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([]);
        expect(report.ok).toBe(true);
      } finally {
        await Promise.all([closeDb(connections.api), closeDb(connections.auth)]);
      }
      const off = await cli(["audit-verify"], { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "" });
      expect(off.code, off.text).toBe(0);
      const bare = await cli(["audit-verify"], { DATABASE_URL_API: process.env.DATABASE_URL_API!, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: process.env.DATABASE_URL_AUTH! }, false);
      expect(bare.code, bare.text).toBe(0);
    });

    test("a confirmed row changed by the owner with the chain and the head recomputed fails on its step-up alone: its params, its target, its session, its hash with its params, or its time past the challenge's expiry", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      const otherParams = { params: { all: true } };
      const changes: [string, Record<string, unknown>, RegExp][] = [
        ["its params", { metadata: otherParams }, /^its step-up's action hash is not the hash of its action, target and params$/],
        ["its target", { targetId: s.c.handle }, /^its step-up's action hash is not the hash of its action, target and params$/],
        ["its session", { staffSession: s.b.handle }, /^its step-up's challenge was not issued for this action in this session$/],
        [
          "its params and its action hash together",
          { metadata: otherParams, actionHash: await stepUpActionHash({ action: "staff_session_revoked", target: { type: "staff_session", id: s.b.handle }, params: otherParams.params }) },
          /^its step-up's challenge was not issued for this action in this session$/,
        ],
        ["its time, past the challenge's expiry", { createdAt: new Date(s.first.createdAt.getTime() + 11 * 60_000) }, /^its step-up's challenge had expired when the row was written$/],
      ];
      for (const [label, change, message] of changes) {
        await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
          await tx.update(auditLog).set(change).where(eq(auditLog.id, s.first.id));
          await rechainFrom(tx, s.first.chainSeq);
          const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
          expect(report.problems, label).toEqual([{ place: s.first.chainSeq, message: expect.stringMatching(message) }]);
        });
      }
      // Nothing of it outlives the rollbacks.
      const connections = ownConnections();
      try {
        expect((await auditVerify(connections, [])).problems).toEqual([]);
      } finally {
        await Promise.all([closeDb(connections.api), closeDb(connections.auth)]);
      }
    });

    test("an assertion moved to another row fails there, on its binding and as a challenge used twice", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        // The first row's assertion, signed by the same key in the same session, on the second row: only the binding of
        // its target, and the challenge's second use, give it away.
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ stepUp: s.first.stepUp }).where(eq(auditLog.id, s.second.id));
        await rechainFrom(tx, s.second.chainSeq);
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([
          { place: s.second.chainSeq, message: "its step-up's challenge was not issued for this action in this session" },
          { place: s.second.chainSeq, message: `its step-up's challenge was already used at place ${s.first.chainSeq}` },
        ]);
      });
    });

    test("a row of a step-up action without a confirmation fails, whatever its actor: a staff account, a demoted one, the system", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      const { user: demoted } = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      await authDb.update(users).set({ role: "user" }).where(eq(users.id, demoted.id));
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const places: number[] = [];
        for (const actor of [s.user.id, demoted.id, actorId]) {
          const [row] = await tx
            .insert(auditLog)
            .values({ actorId: actor, action: "staff_session_revoked", targetType: "staff_session", targetId: randomUUID(), staffSession: randomUUID(), metadata: { params: {} } })
            .returning({ chainSeq: auditLog.chainSeq });
          places.push(row!.chainSeq);
        }
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual(places.map((place) => ({ place, message: "its action, staff_session_revoked, needs a step-up, and it carries none" })));
      });
    });

    test("a confirmation whose key belongs to another account than the row's actor fails, as one whose key records another origin or relying party ID", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      const { user: other } = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ actorId: other.id }).where(eq(auditLog.id, s.first.id));
        await rechainFrom(tx, s.first.chainSeq);
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([{ place: s.first.chainSeq, message: `its step-up's key ${s.keyId} belongs to another account than its actor` }]);
      });
      // The key's recorded origin and relying party ID, which the owner can change too: the confirmation was made for
      // the ones the key was enrolled with, never checked against the console's configuration.
      for (const [label, change, message] of [
        ["origin", { origin: "http://console.example:8090" }, "its step-up's client data is not a webauthn.get from the origin recorded on its key"],
        ["relying party ID", { rpId: "console.example" }, "its step-up's authenticator data does not name the relying party ID recorded on its key"],
      ] as const) {
        await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
          await tx.update(staffKeys).set(change).where(eq(staffKeys.id, s.keyId));
          const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
          expect(report.problems, label).toEqual([
            { place: s.first.chainSeq, message },
            { place: s.second.chainSeq, message },
          ]);
        });
      }
    });

    test("a signature that does not verify with the key's public key fails", { timeout: 60_000 }, async () => {
      const s = await confirmedRevocations();
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const stepUp = s.first.stepUp as { authenticatorData: string; clientDataJSON: string; signature: string };
        const signature = Buffer.from(stepUp.signature, "base64url");
        signature[signature.length - 1] = signature[signature.length - 1]! ^ 0xff;
        await tx.update(auditLog).set({ stepUp: { ...stepUp, signature: signature.toString("base64url") } }).where(eq(auditLog.id, s.first.id));
        await rechainFrom(tx, s.first.chainSeq);
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([{ place: s.first.chainSeq, message: `its step-up's signature does not verify with the public key of key ${s.keyId}` }]);
      });
    });
  });

  describe("staff keys", () => {
    test("a key without its staff_key_added row fails, naming the key", async () => {
      const { user } = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        // Only the owner can plant one: the auth role cannot insert a key, and add_staff_key writes the row with it.
        const [key] = await tx
          .insert(staffKeys)
          .values({ userId: user.id, credentialId: randomUUID(), publicKey: "cose-key", name: "planted", origin: TEST_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, rpId: "console.localhost" })
          .returning({ id: staffKeys.id });
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, []);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([{ place: null, message: `staff key ${key!.id} has no staff_key_added row` }]);
      });
    });

    test("a key enrolled after the head a run read, before it read the keys, is left to the next run, which checks it", { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
      const connections = ownConnections();
      try {
        // The keys are read on the auth role right after the head; a key enrolled between the two has its staff_key_added
        // row beyond the head this run read, so the run leaves it to the next instead of calling it a problem.
        let enrolled: string | undefined;
        const between = {
          select: (fields: Parameters<Db["select"]>[0]) => ({
            from: (table: typeof staffKeys) => ({
              then: (resolve: (rows: unknown) => unknown, reject: (err: unknown) => unknown) =>
                newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo)
                  .then((added) => {
                    enrolled = added.key.id;
                    return connections.auth.select(fields!).from(table);
                  })
                  .then(resolve, reject),
            }),
          }),
        } as unknown as Db;
        const report = await auditVerify({ api: connections.api, auth: between }, []);
        expect(enrolled).toBeDefined();
        expect(report).toMatchObject({ ok: true, keysLeftToNextRun: 1, problems: [] });
        // The next run reads a head beyond the key's row, and checks the key.
        const next = await auditVerify(connections, []);
        expect(next).toMatchObject({ ok: true, keysLeftToNextRun: 0, problems: [] });
        expect(next.keysChecked).toBe(report.keysChecked);
      } finally {
        await Promise.all([closeDb(connections.api), closeDb(connections.auth)]);
      }
    });

    test("a key with a second staff_key_added row fails, naming both places", async () => {
      const { key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const [first] = await apiDb.select({ seq: auditLog.chainSeq }).from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.keyId, key.id));
      // The API role can insert any action; a second row claiming the key's addition is refused by audit-verify.
      await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
        const [second] = await tx.insert(auditLog).values({ actorId, action: "staff_key_added", targetType: "staff_key", targetId: key.id, keyId: key.id }).returning();
        const report = await checkAuditRecord(tx, [], authDb);
        expect(report.problems).toEqual([{ place: null, message: `staff key ${key.id} has 2 staff_key_added rows (places ${first!.seq}, ${second!.chainSeq})` }]);
      });
    });
  });

  describe("the command line", () => {
    test("audit-verify passes the same with the console off and on, and needs nothing of the console's configuration", async () => {
      const head = await readHead();
      const envs: Record<string, string>[] = [{ CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "" }, { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "", CONSOLE_RP_ID: "" }, { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: TEST_CONSOLE_ORIGIN }];
      for (const env of envs) {
        const run = await cli(["audit-verify", `${head.seq}:${head.hash}`], env);
        expect(run.code, JSON.stringify(env)).toBe(0);
        expect(run.text).toContain(`the chain holds: ${head.seq} rows, from place 1 to the head ${head.seq}:${head.hash}`);
        expect(run.text).toContain("1 kept place checked; 0 rows after the newest kept place are not yet anchored");
      }
    });

    test("audit-verify and audit-head run given the database URLs alone: no secret, no other setting, and a console setting the API refuses changes nothing", async () => {
      const head = await readHead();
      const urls = { DATABASE_URL_API: process.env.DATABASE_URL_API!, DATABASE_URL_AUTH: process.env.DATABASE_URL_AUTH! };
      const envs: Record<string, string>[] = [
        urls,
        // A final slash, which the API's configuration refuses in CONSOLE_ORIGIN.
        { ...urls, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "https://console.example/" },
        // The console on the app's origin, which it refuses too.
        { ...urls, APP_ORIGIN: process.env.APP_ORIGIN!, CONSOLE_ORIGIN: process.env.APP_ORIGIN! },
      ];
      for (const env of envs) {
        const run = await cli(["audit-verify", `${head.seq}:${head.hash}`], env, false);
        expect(run.code, JSON.stringify(Object.keys(env))).toBe(0);
        expect(run.text).toContain(`the chain holds: ${head.seq} rows, from place 1 to the head ${head.seq}:${head.hash}`);
      }
      const headRun = await cli(["audit-head"], { DATABASE_URL_API: urls.DATABASE_URL_API }, false);
      expect(headRun.code).toBe(0);
      expect(headRun.text).toMatch(new RegExp(`^${head.seq}:${head.hash} `));
    });

    test("audit-verify exits 1 and names the place at fault when a kept place does not match", async () => {
      const head = await readHead();
      const run = await cli(["audit-verify", `1:${await hashAt(1)}`, `${head.seq}:${"f".repeat(64)}`]);
      expect(run.code).toBe(1);
      expect(run.text).toContain("audit-verify: FAILED");
      expect(run.text).toContain(`place ${head.seq}: the kept place ${head.seq}:${"f".repeat(64)} no longer matches`);
    });

    test("audit-head prints the newest place, its hash and its time, and they are what audit_head holds", async () => {
      const head = await readHead();
      const [newest] = await apiDb.select().from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, head.seq));
      const run = await cli(["audit-head"], { CONSOLE_ORIGIN: "" });
      expect(run.code).toBe(0);
      expect(run.text).toBe(`${head.seq}:${head.hash} ${newest!.createdAt.toISOString()}`);
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
    const first = await explore("?limit=2", reader.b);
    expect(pageIds(first)).toEqual(order.slice(0, 2));
    expect(first).toMatchObject({ computedAt: asOf.toISOString(), signInForMore: false });
    const cursor = encodeURIComponent(first.nextCursor!);

    // Any cursor, a real one or not, asks for more than the first page, which needs an account.
    for (const query of [`?cursor=${cursor}`, `?limit=2&cursor=${cursor}`, "?cursor=not-a-cursor"]) {
      const refused = await app.request(`/api/timeline/explore${query}`);
      expect(refused.status, query).toBe(401);
      expect(refused.headers.get("cache-control"), query).toBe("no-store");
      expect(await errorOf(refused), query).toMatchObject({ code: "unauthenticated", message: "Sign in to see more of Explore." });
    }

    const second = await explore(`?limit=2&cursor=${cursor}`, reader.b);
    const third = await explore(`?limit=2&cursor=${encodeURIComponent(second.nextCursor!)}`, reader.b);
    expect([...pageIds(first), ...pageIds(second), ...pageIds(third)]).toEqual(order);
    expect(third).toMatchObject({ nextCursor: null, computedAt: asOf.toISOString(), signInForMore: false });
    // Signed in, a cursor that is not one is the request's fault, not a reason to sign in.
    const bad = await reader.b.fetch("/api/timeline/explore?cursor=not-a-cursor");
    expect(bad.status).toBe(400);
    expect((await errorOf(bad)).code).toBe("invalid_request");
  });
```
