### Create `apps/api/src/lib/lock-bounds.ts`

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";

/**
 * The lock waits of a transaction that carries out an action a staff key confirmed (3a design, section 7, Step-up; 3c
 * design, section 7.5), shared by the auth module, the moderation module and the command lines. audit-verify refuses for
 * good an audit row stamped at or after its step-up challenge's expiry, and the row is stamped only once the transaction
 * holds the audit head, so every wait before it must end in time. This file has no entry point of its own, so every
 * bundle can include it.
 */

/** Whether an error is PostgreSQL's, with this SQLSTATE, however deeply the driver wrapped it. */
function hasSqlState(err: unknown, code: string): boolean {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    if (typeof current === "object" && (current as { code?: unknown }).code === code) return true;
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return false;
}

/** True for PostgreSQL's lock_not_available: a lock_timeout ran out, and the transaction that gave up has changed nothing. */
export function isLockNotAvailable(err: unknown): boolean {
  return hasSqlState(err, "55P03");
}

/** True for PostgreSQL's deadlock_detected: this transaction was chosen to give way, and has changed nothing. */
export function isDeadlock(err: unknown): boolean {
  return hasSqlState(err, "40P01");
}

/**
 * Bounds every lock wait of a confirmed action's transaction: lock_timeout becomes the share of what is left of the
 * challenge's life, by the database's clock, that one of `waits` waits may take, and at most 15 seconds, so the waits the
 * transaction may meet all end before the expiry. `waits` is the number of locks it may have to wait for. False when
 * nothing is left, or less than a millisecond, which lock_timeout would read as no limit at all; nothing is set then. The
 * bound only aims to end the transaction in time: the statement that writes the audit row checks the clock itself.
 */
export async function boundLockWaits(tx: Pick<DbTx, "execute">, expiresAt: Date, waits: number): Promise<boolean> {
  if (!Number.isInteger(waits) || waits < 1) throw new Error("boundLockWaits takes the number of waits to bound: a positive whole number");
  const [left] = await tx.execute<{ ms: string }>(
    sql`select floor(least(15000, (${expiresAt.getTime()}::numeric - extract(epoch from clock_timestamp()) * 1000) / ${waits}::numeric))::bigint::text as ms`,
  );
  const ms = Number(left!.ms);
  if (!(ms >= 1)) return false;
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${ms}ms`}::text, true)`);
  return true;
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/context.ts`

```ts
import { ModerationErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { SocialForModeration } from "../social";

/** The moderation codes plus the shared ones the module also raises. */
export type ModerationErrorKind = ModerationErrorCode | "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "rate_limited" | "service_unavailable";
export type ModerationErrorStatus = 400 | 403 | 404 | 409 | 422 | 429 | 503;

/** What each code answers with over HTTP (3c design, section 10). */
const STATUS: Record<ModerationErrorKind, ModerationErrorStatus> = {
  already_reported: 409,
  case_changed: 409,
  case_closed: 409,
  staff_recused: 403,
  staff_target: 403,
  admin_required: 403,
  decision_cap: 429,
  profile_changed: 409,
  snapshot_mismatch: 409,
  snapshot_erased: 409,
  text_not_found: 409,
  invalid_decision: 422,
  not_found: 404,
  invalid_request: 400,
  rate_limited: 429,
  service_unavailable: 503,
};

// The first three are written for the person reporting; the rest for staff, whose console words them again for the screen.
const MESSAGES: Record<ModerationErrorKind, string> = {
  already_reported: "You already reported this; it is being looked at.",
  case_changed: "The case changed since it was opened. Open it again.",
  case_closed: "The case changed at that moment. Try again.",
  staff_recused: "You cannot act on this case: you, or an account close to you, are a party to it.",
  staff_target: "A final decision cannot restrict a staff account. Staff are disciplined by demotion.",
  admin_required: "Only an admin can take this decision.",
  decision_cap: "You have reached the limit on decisions for now. Try again later.",
  profile_changed: "The profile changed since the snapshot was taken. Take a fresh snapshot and decide again.",
  snapshot_mismatch: "The snapshot is not the one this case holds.",
  snapshot_erased: "The snapshot was erased. Take a fresh one and decide again.",
  text_not_found: "A text of this decision is not saved, or was used already. Save it again.",
  invalid_decision: "This decision cannot stand as it is.",
  not_found: "Not found.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  rate_limited: "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
};

/** An expected failure of a moderation flow. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class ModerationError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: ModerationErrorKind,
    readonly status: ModerationErrorStatus = STATUS[code],
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** Set for rate_limited so the response can carry Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ModerationError";
  }
}

export function moderationErrorMessage(code: ModerationErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/** Whether a message the database raised is one of the module's codes, which the triggers raise as their message. */
export function isModerationErrorCode(message: string): message is ModerationErrorCode {
  return ModerationErrorCode.safeParse(message).success;
}

export interface ModerationDeps {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The social module's interface: the locks on profile rows and the reads evidence is copied from. */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  config: Config;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/decide.ts`

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { CaseDecidedParams } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_VERSION, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import { boundLockWaits, isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { appendConfirmedAudit, caseTarget, insertAction, insertDecision, raisedMessage } from "./repo";

/**
 * The confirmed decision's transaction (3c design, section 7.5, step 3). The API writes the decision's row, one row for
 * each measure or reversal and, last, the audit row; the database's triggers lock, check, complete and apply them
 * (migration 0016), and its deferred check refuses at commit a decision whose audit row does not name exactly it.
 */

/** A decision that committed, or why none did: the confirming account or key ended, or the challenge's time ran out. */
export type DecideOutcome = { decisionId: string } | "ended" | "late";

/**
 * The lock waits one decision may meet: the subject's profile, the case, the deciding account's row, the cap's advisory
 * lock, up to three texts, the subject's account row, the post, up to four images, the key and the audit head. A decision
 * that seals, lifts a seal or ends one also locks every image row its seals list; that number has no bound and is not
 * counted, and the audit row's own check of the clock rolls back a transaction that outlasts the challenge.
 */
const DECISION_WAITS = 15;

/** A transaction that met a deadlock or a lock timeout is run once more only while more than this much of the challenge is left. */
const RETRY_MARGIN_MS = 60_000;

/**
 * POST /api/staff/cases/:case/decisions, once its step-up verified: records the decision the session's key confirmed.
 * In one transaction on the API's pool, in this order:
 *   1. every lock wait is bounded by a fifteenth of what is left of the challenge, at most 15 seconds; with under a
 *      millisecond left nothing is written ("late");
 *   2. the subject account's profile row FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the transaction's first lock, so two decisions about one
 *      account run one after the other while likes and follows of others never wait for it;
 *   3. the decision's row, whose triggers lock the case and check everything about it;
 *   4. one row for each measure or reversal, in the params' order, whose triggers derive what the post and its images
 *      now are;
 *   5. last, the audit row, through public.append_confirmed_audit, with the params exactly as confirmed and the
 *      decision's id.
 * A deadlock, or a lock timeout the bound cut short, runs the transaction once more with the same confirmation while more
 * than a minute of the challenge is left: nothing was written, and no other request can use the spent challenge. Every
 * code a trigger raises is thrown as its ModerationError.
 */
export async function decide(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never decides a case: that would be a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "case_decided" || confirmed.target.type !== "case" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) {
    throw new Error("a decision needs a step-up that confirmed it");
  }
  const params = CaseDecidedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  // A decision is made under the texts the API serves now: the redress texts always, and the rulebook unless it is a
  // correction, which carries the version of the decision it corrects.
  if (params.redressVersion !== REDRESS_VERSION || (params.kind !== "correction" && params.rulesVersion !== RULES_VERSION)) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");

  const caseId = confirmed.target.id;
  const target = await caseTarget(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!target) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  // A case's target never changes, and a post's author never does, so the subject is read before the transaction.
  const subject = target.type === "account" ? target.id : await deps.social.postAuthor(target.id);

  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx): Promise<DecideOutcome> => {
        if (!(await boundLockWaits(tx, confirmed.expiresAt, DECISION_WAITS))) return "late";
        if (subject !== null) await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [subject], "no key update");
        const decisionId = randomUUID();
        await insertDecision(tx, { id: decisionId, caseId, decidedBy: session.userId, params });
        for (const action of params.actions) await insertAction(tx, decisionId, action);
        await appendConfirmedAudit(tx, {
          actorId: session.userId,
          keyId: confirmed.keyId,
          action: "case_decided",
          targetType: "case",
          targetId: caseId,
          metadata: { params: confirmed.params, decisionId },
          staffSession: session.handle,
          actionHash: confirmed.actionHash,
          stepUp: confirmed.assertion,
          requestId: ctx.requestId,
          expiresAt: confirmed.expiresAt,
        });
        return { decisionId };
      });
    } catch (err) {
      const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_ended") return "ended";
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_late") return "late";
      if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) throw new ModerationError(refusal);
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt > 1 || confirmed.expiresAt.getTime() - deps.now().getTime() <= RETRY_MARGIN_MS) return "late";
    }
  }
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/index.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/moderation/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the architecture test
 * fails the build if another file reaches into it.
 *
 * The moderation module (3c design, section 5) runs on the API's role and owns the moderation tables: intakes and their
 * items, cases, decisions and their ledger of measures, evidence snapshots and staff texts. It inserts rows; the database
 * checks them, derives every restriction from them and refuses at commit what cannot stand. It reaches the other modules
 * only through the interfaces they export, never names an image row, and never sees the auth schema.
 */
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { SocialForModeration } from "../social";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { decide, type DecideOutcome } from "./decide";

export { ModerationError } from "./context";
export type { ModerationDeps, ModerationErrorKind } from "./context";
export type { DecideOutcome } from "./decide";

/** What the staff module needs from this one: the console's operations on cases, which its routes run behind the staff gate. */
export interface ModerationForStaff {
  /**
   * Records the decision a step-up confirmed, in one transaction with its audit row. "ended" when the confirming account
   * or key no longer opens anything, "late" when the challenge's time ran out; neither writes anything.
   */
  decide(session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }): Promise<DecideOutcome>;
}

export interface CreateModerationOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The social module's interface for cases: socialForModeration(apiDb). */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createModeration(options: CreateModerationOptions) {
  const deps: ModerationDeps = {
    apiDb: options.apiDb,
    social: options.social,
    config: options.config,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  const forStaff: ModerationForStaff = {
    decide: (session, confirmed, ctx) => decide(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
  };
}

export type Moderation = ReturnType<typeof createModeration>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/intake.ts`

```ts
import { createHash, randomBytes, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { laneFor, snapshotDigest, type Lane, type RuleId, type TdbCategory } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { ModerationError, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { insertIntake, insertItem, insertSnapshot, isSerializationFailure, latestSnapshot, openCase, snapshotTime, violatedUniqueConstraint } from "./repo";

/**
 * Taking in a report, a notice or a moderator's own finding (3c design, section 7.1, step 4): one intake, one item for
 * each target it names, each item in exactly one open case, and the first copy of each target as evidence. The routes
 * that validate a request and resolve its targets come with the reports themselves; this is the transaction they run.
 */

/** What an intake alleges and who sent it: the ground's columns of the intake's row. */
export interface IntakeGround {
  kind: "user" | "finding";
  channel: "signed_in" | "signed_out" | "staff";
  /** The signed-in reporter; never set on the path for child sexual abuse material, which records no sender. */
  reporterId: string | null;
  /** The staff account behind a finding. */
  findingBy: string | null;
  /** The id under which the auth module keeps a signed-out notifier's name and address. */
  contactId: string | null;
  ruleId: RuleId | null;
  allegesIllegal: boolean;
  csam: boolean;
  category: TdbCategory;
  categoryKeyword: string | null;
  citedLaw: string | null;
  explanation: string | null;
  bonaFide: boolean;
}

/** A target that is live: a post by its id, or an account by its id with the handle it was named by. `position` is its place among the targets named, from 1. */
export type LiveTarget =
  | { type: "post"; id: string; position: number; mediaId?: string | null }
  | { type: "account"; id: string; position: number; namedHandle: string };

/** A target with nothing live: a link to a post that names no row or a deleted one, or a handle that names no account. It is stored as answered at once. */
export type DeadTarget = { type: "post"; id: string; position: number } | { type: "account"; position: number; namedHandle: string };

export interface IntakeRequest {
  ground: IntakeGround;
  live: readonly LiveTarget[];
  dead?: readonly DeadTarget[];
}

export interface RecordedItem {
  id: string;
  position: number;
  targetType: "post" | "account";
  targetId: string;
  /** Null for a target with nothing live. */
  caseId: string | null;
  seq: number | null;
  lane: Lane;
}

export interface IntakeRecorded {
  intakeId: string;
  /** The public reference: N- and ten base32 characters. */
  ref: string;
  /** The notice's token, for a signed-out notice and for every notice on the CSAM path: shown once, and stored only as its sha256. */
  token: string | null;
  /** Whether the intake's items are suspect: it is on the CSAM path, or a finding citing R2. */
  suspect: boolean;
  items: RecordedItem[];
}

/** How often the transaction is run again after a case closed under it, a deadlock or a lock timeout: in each nothing was written. */
const RETRIES = 3;
/** How often one transaction asks for a target's open case before it starts over. */
const CASE_READS = 3;
/**
 * The longest the intake waits for a lock. A case's row is held by a decision for as long as that decision's
 * transaction runs, which for a seal over thousands of images is seconds; an intake that waited longer starts over.
 */
const LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

const BASE32 = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567";

/** A fresh public reference: N- and ten base32 characters from 50 random bits. */
function newRef(): string {
  const bytes = randomBytes(7);
  // 48 bits and two more: 50 in all, which a JavaScript number holds exactly.
  const bits = bytes.readUIntBE(0, 6) * 4 + (bytes[6]! & 3);
  let ref = "";
  // 50 bits, five at a time from the top.
  for (let shift = 45; shift >= 0; shift -= 5) ref += BASE32[Math.floor(bits / 2 ** shift) % 32];
  return `N-${ref}`;
}

/** Whether an intake's items are suspect, as the attach trigger forces it: the CSAM path, or a finding citing R2. */
export const isSuspect = (ground: IntakeGround) => ground.csam || ground.ruleId === "R2";

/**
 * The live targets of a suspect intake with the items korbat adds: a post's card shows the images of the post it
 * quotes, so a report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is a report about both. Each
 * quoted post that the request does not name itself becomes a target of its own, at the position of the item it was
 * added for plus 10 (the lowest such position when several named posts quote it). One level only, as a card draws one
 * quote deep: an added target brings none of its own. Read outside any transaction; a post's quote never changes.
 */
export async function withAddedTargets(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "social">, live: readonly LiveTarget[]): Promise<LiveTarget[]> {
  const named = new Set(live.filter((target) => target.type === "post").map((target) => target.id));
  const added = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const target of live) {
    if (target.type !== "post" || target.position > 10) continue;
    const quoted = (await deps.social.postRef(target.id))?.quoteOfId;
    if (!quoted || named.has(quoted)) continue;
    added.set(quoted, Math.min(added.get(quoted) ?? target.position, target.position));
  }
  return [...live, ...[...added].map(([id, position]): LiveTarget => ({ type: "post", id, position: position + 10 }))];
}

/** Thrown inside the transaction to roll it back and run it again: the case a target was read into closed before the read found one. */
class StartOver extends Error {}

/** A case's targets in one order for every intake: by kind (posts before accounts, as the database orders the two) and then by id. */
const byTarget = (a: LiveTarget, b: LiveTarget) => (a.type !== b.type ? (a.type === "post" ? -1 : 1) : a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0);

/**
 * Stores one intake in one transaction, which changes nothing unless it commits. In this order:
 *   1. a signed-in reporter's profile row, FOR KEY SHARE, refusing a missing or deleted account;
 *   2. the intake's row, with a fresh reference and, for a signed-out or CSAM notice, the hash of a fresh token;
 *   3. for each live target, in the targets' order: its open case (opened when there is none) and then its item, which
 *      the attach trigger numbers into the case, so every intake takes its cases in one order and two notices that name
 *      the same targets never deadlock; only then the captures, posts in id order, each under a share lock on its post,
 *      so none holds a post while it waits for a case;
 *   4. a snapshot for each case that holds none yet, or, for an account, whose newest one differs from the account now;
 *   5. for each target with nothing live, an item with no case, answered at once.
 * It is run again, up to three times, when an item's case closed in between (the attach trigger says so), on a deadlock
 * and on a lock timeout; when the last run fails the same way the answer is case_closed. A signed-in reporter who already
 * has an item on the same ground in a target's open case is answered already_reported.
 */
export async function recordIntake(deps: ModerationDeps, request: IntakeRequest): Promise<IntakeRecorded> {
  const suspect = isSuspect(request.ground);
  const live = suspect ? await withAddedTargets(deps, request.live) : [...request.live];
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => recordIn(deps, tx, { ...request, live }, suspect));
    } catch (err) {
      const constraint = violatedUniqueConstraint(err);
      if (constraint === "intake_items_reporter_once") throw new ModerationError("already_reported");
      // A reference another intake already has: one in 2^50 for each pair. The next run draws a new one.
      const startOver = err instanceof StartOver || isSerializationFailure(err) || isDeadlock(err) || isLockNotAvailable(err) || constraint === "intakes_ref_unique";
      if (!startOver) throw err;
      if (attempt >= RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("case_closed");
    }
  }
}

async function recordIn(deps: ModerationDeps, tx: DbTx, request: IntakeRequest, suspect: boolean): Promise<IntakeRecorded> {
  const { ground } = request;
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);

  // 1.
  if (ground.reporterId !== null) await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [ground.reporterId], "key share", true);

  // 2. The token is stored only as its hash; the answer carries it once.
  const ref = newRef();
  const token = ground.channel === "signed_out" || ground.csam ? randomBytes(32).toString("base64url") : null;
  const intakeId = await insertIntake(tx, { ...ground, ref, lookupHash: token === null ? null : createHash("sha256").update(token).digest("hex") });
  const lane = laneFor({ ruleId: ground.ruleId, allegesIllegal: ground.allegesIllegal, csam: ground.csam, category: ground.category });

  // 3. First every case with its item, in the targets' order.
  const items: RecordedItem[] = [];
  const cases = new Map<LiveTarget, string>();
  for (const target of [...request.live].sort(byTarget)) {
    let caseId: string | null = null;
    for (let read = 0; read < CASE_READS && caseId === null; read++) caseId = await openCase(tx, target.type, target.id);
    // A live target's item is never stored without a case.
    if (caseId === null) throw new StartOver();
    cases.set(target, caseId);
    const item = await insertItem(tx, {
      intakeId,
      caseId,
      targetType: target.type,
      targetId: target.id,
      position: target.position,
      lane,
      mediaId: target.type === "post" ? (target.mediaId ?? null) : null,
      namedHandle: target.type === "account" ? target.namedHandle.toLowerCase() : null,
    });
    items.push({ id: item.id, position: target.position, targetType: target.type, targetId: target.id, caseId, seq: item.seq, lane });
  }

  // Then the captures and, 4., the snapshots. The time is the transaction's start, which the snapshots' trigger stamps.
  const takenAt = await snapshotTime(tx);
  for (const [target, caseId] of cases) {
    const before = await latestSnapshot(tx, caseId);
    if (target.type === "post") {
      const post = await deps.social.capturePost(tx, target.id);
      if (!post) throw new Error("a post that an intake names has no row");
      if (before !== null) continue;
      await storeSnapshot(tx, takenAt, {
        caseId,
        targetType: "post",
        targetId: target.id,
        authorHandle: post.authorHandle,
        postState: post.state,
        postCreatedAt: post.createdAt.toISOString(),
        replyToId: post.replyToId,
        quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
        body: post.body,
        // The image rows are the media module's, which hands a post's images over when it holds them for the case; until
        // the intake is given that, a post's snapshot lists none.
        media: [],
        displayName: null,
        bio: null,
        handle: null,
      });
    } else {
      const profile = await deps.social.captureProfile(tx, target.id);
      if (!profile) throw new Error("an account that an intake names has no row");
      if (before !== null && before.displayName === profile.displayName && before.bio === profile.bio && before.handle === profile.handle) continue;
      await storeSnapshot(tx, takenAt, {
        caseId,
        targetType: "account",
        targetId: target.id,
        authorHandle: profile.handle,
        postState: null,
        postCreatedAt: null,
        replyToId: null,
        quoteOfId: null,
        body: null,
        media: null,
        displayName: profile.displayName,
        bio: profile.bio,
        handle: profile.handle,
      });
    }
  }

  // 5. An account's link that names nothing gets an id that names nothing either, whether or not a profile holds or once
  // held the handle: no stored id ties an old handle to its account.
  for (const target of request.dead ?? []) {
    const targetId = target.type === "post" ? target.id : randomUUID();
    const item = await insertItem(tx, {
      intakeId,
      caseId: null,
      targetType: target.type,
      targetId,
      position: target.position,
      lane,
      mediaId: null,
      namedHandle: target.type === "account" ? target.namedHandle.toLowerCase() : null,
    });
    items.push({ id: item.id, position: target.position, targetType: target.type, targetId, caseId: null, seq: null, lane });
  }
  items.sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position);
  return { intakeId, ref, token, suspect, items };
}

type SnapshotContent = Omit<Parameters<typeof insertSnapshot>[1], "salt" | "digest">;

/**
 * One snapshot: a salt of the server's own, and the digest over the salt, the time and everything copied. The time in
 * the digest is the one the database stamps the row with; when the two differ the transaction is rolled back, since the
 * stored row would not recompute to its digest.
 */
async function storeSnapshot(tx: DbTx, takenAt: string, content: SnapshotContent): Promise<void> {
  const salt = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");
  const digest = await snapshotDigest({
    salt,
    targetType: content.targetType,
    targetId: content.targetId,
    takenAt,
    authorHandle: content.authorHandle,
    postState: content.postState,
    postCreatedAt: content.postCreatedAt,
    replyToId: content.replyToId,
    quoteOfId: content.quoteOfId,
    body: content.body,
    media: content.media,
    displayName: content.displayName,
    bio: content.bio,
    handle: content.handle,
  });
  const stored = await insertSnapshot(tx, { ...content, salt, digest });
  if (stored.takenAt !== takenAt) throw new Error("a snapshot was stamped at another time than its digest covers");
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/repo.ts`

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { ActionKind, CaseDecidedParams, Lane, StaffStoredAssertion } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";

/**
 * The SQL statements of the moderation module, on the korbat_api pool (3c design, sections 5 and 6). The module inserts
 * rows; migrator-owned triggers check them, force the columns the API must not choose, and derive every restriction from
 * them. So each insert here names only what the API supplies: the database sets the rest whatever an insert said (a time,
 * a number in a case, who a report came from), and a column left out can never be mistaken for one the API chose. That is
 * why the inserts are written as SQL: a query builder would name every column of the table.
 */

/** What a statement runs through: the pool, or a transaction. */
type Runner = Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">;

const rows = async <T>(q: Runner, query: ReturnType<typeof sql>): Promise<T[]> => (await q.execute(query)) as unknown as T[];

/** A timestamptz expression as the text Date.prototype.toISOString writes: UTC, to the millisecond. The expression is written here, never input. */
const iso = (expression: string) => sql.raw(`to_char(${expression} at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"')`);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what the database raised

/** The first of the driver's errors in the chain that carries a SQLSTATE; drizzle wraps the driver's error as a cause. */
function driverError(err: unknown): { code: string; message: unknown; constraint_name?: unknown } | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    if (typeof current === "object" && typeof (current as { code?: unknown }).code === "string") return current as { code: string; message: unknown; constraint_name?: unknown };
    current = (current as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  }
  return null;
}

/** The message of an exception a trigger or a function raised as its code (SQLSTATE P0001); null for anything else. */
export function raisedMessage(err: unknown): string | null {
  const raised = driverError(err);
  return raised?.code === "P0001" && typeof raised.message === "string" ? raised.message : null;
}

/** True for a serialization failure (SQLSTATE 40001): the attach trigger raises it when an item's case closed in between. */
export function isSerializationFailure(err: unknown): boolean {
  return driverError(err)?.code === "40001";
}

/** The constraint a unique violation names (SQLSTATE 23505), or null for anything else. */
export function violatedUniqueConstraint(err: unknown): string | null {
  const raised = driverError(err);
  return raised?.code === "23505" && typeof raised.constraint_name === "string" ? raised.constraint_name : null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- intakes, items and cases

export type TargetType = "post" | "account";

/** One report, notice or finding as the intake's transaction stores it; the trigger sets when it was received and its receipt's state. */
export interface IntakeRow {
  kind: "user" | "finding";
  ref: string;
  /** The sha256 hex of the notice's token, for a signed-out notice and for every notice on the CSAM path. */
  lookupHash: string | null;
  channel: "signed_in" | "signed_out" | "staff";
  reporterId: string | null;
  findingBy: string | null;
  contactId: string | null;
  ruleId: string | null;
  allegesIllegal: boolean;
  csam: boolean;
  category: string;
  categoryKeyword: string | null;
  citedLaw: string | null;
  explanation: string | null;
  bonaFide: boolean;
}

export async function insertIntake(tx: DbTx, row: IntakeRow): Promise<string> {
  const [inserted] = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    tx,
    sql`insert into intakes (kind, ref, lookup_hash, channel, reporter_id, finding_by, contact_id, rule_id, alleges_illegal, csam, category, category_keyword, cited_law, explanation, bona_fide)
        values (${row.kind}::intake_kind, ${row.ref}, ${row.lookupHash}, ${row.channel}::intake_channel, ${row.reporterId}::uuid, ${row.findingBy}::uuid, ${row.contactId}::uuid,
                ${row.ruleId}, ${row.allegesIllegal}::boolean, ${row.csam}::boolean, ${row.category}, ${row.categoryKeyword}, ${row.citedLaw}, ${row.explanation}, ${row.bonaFide}::boolean)
        returning id`,
  );
  return inserted!.id;
}

/**
 * The target's open case, opened when there is none: an insert that does nothing on a conflict (the API role holds no
 * UPDATE on cases, so it could not do anything else), then a read of the open case in a statement of its own, which
 * sees a case another transaction committed while the insert waited. Null when the read finds none: a decision closed
 * the case after the insert, and the caller runs both again.
 */
export async function openCase(tx: DbTx, targetType: TargetType, targetId: string): Promise<string | null> {
  await tx.execute(sql`insert into cases (target_type, target_id) values (${targetType}::moderation_target, ${targetId}::uuid) on conflict (target_type, target_id) where closed_at is null do nothing`);
  const [open] = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from cases where target_type = ${targetType}::moderation_target and target_id = ${targetId}::uuid and closed_at is null`);
  return open?.id ?? null;
}

/** One target of an intake. With a case the attach trigger numbers it into the case; without one it is stored as answered at once, not available. */
export interface ItemRow {
  intakeId: string;
  caseId: string | null;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  position: number;
  lane: Lane;
  /** The image the sender pointed at: a hint. */
  mediaId: string | null;
  /** For an account, the handle as it was named, in lower case. */
  namedHandle: string | null;
}

export async function insertItem(tx: DbTx, row: ItemRow): Promise<{ id: string; seq: number | null }> {
  const [inserted] = await rows<{ id: string; seq: number | null }>(
    tx,
    sql`insert into intake_items (intake_id, case_id, target_type, target_id, position, lane, media_id, named_handle, outcome)
        values (${row.intakeId}::uuid, ${row.caseId}::uuid, ${row.targetType}::moderation_target, ${row.targetId}::uuid, ${row.position}::smallint, ${row.lane}::smallint,
                ${row.mediaId}::uuid, ${row.namedHandle}, ${row.caseId === null ? "not_available" : null}::item_outcome)
        returning id, seq`,
  );
  return inserted!;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence

/** The transaction's start to the millisecond, as the snapshots' trigger stamps a snapshot taken in it. */
export async function snapshotTime(tx: DbTx): Promise<string> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ at: string }>(tx, sql`select ${iso("date_trunc('milliseconds', now())")} as at`);
  return row!.at;
}

/**
 * Whether the case holds a snapshot yet, and for an account's case the fields of its newest one. A snapshot's time is its
 * transaction's start to the millisecond, so two snapshots of one case can carry the same time; their ids, which
 * insertSnapshot draws in time order, say which is the newer.
 */
export async function latestSnapshot(tx: DbTx, caseId: string): Promise<{ displayName: string | null; bio: string | null; handle: string | null } | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ display_name: string | null; bio: string | null; handle: string | null }>(
    tx,
    sql`select display_name, bio, handle from evidence_snapshots where case_id = ${caseId}::uuid order by taken_at desc, id desc limit 1`,
  );
  return row ? { displayName: row.display_name, bio: row.bio, handle: row.handle } : null;
}

/** A snapshot as the intake stores it: what was copied, with the salt and the digest the server made over all of it. */
export interface SnapshotRow {
  caseId: string;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  authorHandle: string;
  postState: "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" | "deleted_by_author" | null;
  postCreatedAt: string | null;
  replyToId: string | null;
  quoteOfId: string | null;
  body: string | null;
  media: { id: string; alt: string | null; width: number; height: number }[] | null;
  displayName: string | null;
  bio: string | null;
  handle: string | null;
  salt: string;
  digest: string;
}

/**
 * Stores a snapshot and answers its id with the time the database stamped it, as text to the millisecond. The id is a
 * version 7 uuid, which PostgreSQL draws in time order and never backwards within a session: the newest snapshot of a
 * case is then the one with the latest time and, among those of one millisecond, the greatest id.
 */
export async function insertSnapshot(tx: DbTx, row: SnapshotRow): Promise<{ id: string; takenAt: string }> {
  const [inserted] = await rows<{ id: string; taken_at: string }>(
    tx,
    sql`insert into evidence_snapshots (id, case_id, target_type, target_id, author_handle, post_state, post_created_at, reply_to_id, quote_of_id, body, media, display_name, bio, handle, salt, digest)
        values (uuidv7(), ${row.caseId}::uuid, ${row.targetType}::moderation_target, ${row.targetId}::uuid, ${row.authorHandle}, ${row.postState}::post_state, ${row.postCreatedAt}::timestamptz,
                ${row.replyToId}::uuid, ${row.quoteOfId}::uuid, ${row.body}, ${row.media === null ? null : JSON.stringify(row.media)}::text::jsonb, ${row.displayName}, ${row.bio}, ${row.handle},
                ${row.salt}, ${row.digest})
        returning id, ${iso("taken_at")} as taken_at`,
  );
  return { id: inserted!.id, takenAt: inserted!.taken_at };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- decisions

/** What a case is about, or null when no case has the id. */
export async function caseTarget(q: Runner, caseId: string): Promise<{ type: TargetType; id: string } | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ target_type: TargetType; target_id: string }>(q, sql`select target_type, target_id from cases where id = ${caseId}::uuid`);
  return row ? { type: row.target_type, id: row.target_id } : null;
}

/**
 * The decision's row, from the params its staff key confirmed and the account that decided. The id is the API's, so the
 * audit row can name the decision; everything else the row holds is the triggers'.
 */
export async function insertDecision(tx: DbTx, row: { id: string; caseId: string; decidedBy: string; params: CaseDecidedParams }): Promise<void> {
  const p = row.params;
  await tx.execute(
    sql`insert into decisions (id, case_id, kind, reviews_decision_id, seen_state_version, through_seq, outcome, ground, rule_id, rules_version, redress_version, category, category_keyword,
                               snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, facts_digest, reason_digest, legal_reference_digest, decided_by)
        values (${row.id}::uuid, ${row.caseId}::uuid, ${p.kind}::decision_kind, ${p.reviewsDecisionId}::uuid, ${p.stateVersion}::int, ${p.throughSeq}::int, ${p.outcome}::decision_outcome,
                ${p.ground}::decision_ground, ${p.ruleId}, ${p.rulesVersion}::smallint, ${p.redressVersion}::smallint, ${p.category}, ${p.categoryKeyword},
                ${p.snapshotId}::uuid, ${p.snapshotDigest}, ${p.factsDigest}, ${p.reasonDigest}, ${p.legalReferenceDigest}, ${row.decidedBy}::uuid)`,
  );
}

/** One measure or reversal of a decision. Its target, the measure it lifts and whether it changes anything are the triggers'. */
export async function insertAction(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string, action: { kind: ActionKind; mediaId: string | null }): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`insert into decision_actions (decision_id, kind, media_id) values (${decisionId}::uuid, ${action.kind}::action_kind, ${action.mediaId}::uuid)`);
}

/** The audit row of a confirmed action, as public.append_confirmed_audit writes it. */
export interface ConfirmedAuditRow {
  actorId: string;
  keyId: string;
  action: "case_decided" | "appeals_reviewed" | "identity_revealed";
  targetType: string;
  targetId: string;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
  staffSession: string;
  actionHash: string;
  stepUp: StaffStoredAssertion;
  requestId: string;
  /** The step-up challenge's expiry: the function refuses a row that joins the chain at or after it. */
  expiresAt: Date;
}

/**
 * Writes a confirmed action's audit row through public.append_confirmed_audit, as the last statement of the action's
 * transaction: the function checks that the acting account and its key are still live, writes the row, and refuses it when
 * the challenge had expired by then, which rolls the whole transaction back. The row holds the chain's head until the
 * commit, so nothing that can wait may run after it. Answers the row's place in the chain.
 */
export async function appendConfirmedAudit(tx: DbTx, row: ConfirmedAuditRow): Promise<number> {
  // The jsonb arguments go as text and are cast, so the driver sends them exactly as serialised here.
  const [written] = await rows<{ place: string }>(
    tx,
    sql`select public.append_confirmed_audit(${row.actorId}::uuid, ${row.keyId}::uuid, ${row.action}::text, ${row.targetType}::text, ${row.targetId}::text,
          ${JSON.stringify(row.metadata)}::text::jsonb, ${row.staffSession}::uuid, ${row.actionHash}::text, ${JSON.stringify(row.stepUp)}::text::jsonb,
          ${row.requestId}::text, ${row.expiresAt.getTime()}::bigint)::text as place`,
  );
  return Number(written!.place);
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/staff/cases.ts`

```ts
import type { CaseDecisionResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono, type Context } from "hono";
import { AuthError, type ActiveStaffSession, type AuthForStaff, type StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { ModerationForStaff } from "../moderation";

/**
 * The console's case routes (3c design, sections 5 and 7), a route group the staff routes mount behind the staff gate.
 * Each stands behind requireStaff; one that changes something stands behind requireStaffStepUp as well, which verifies
 * the key's confirmation of exactly what the route is about to do. The handlers only call the moderation module's staff
 * interface and shape the answer: the step-up stays the auth module's, the cases the moderation module's.
 */
export function caseRoutes(auth: AuthForStaff, moderation: ModerationForStaff) {
  const routes = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  /** The session requireStaff read; a route without it in front is a wiring fault, not a refusal. */
  const staffSession = (c: Context<AppEnv>): ActiveStaffSession => {
    const session = c.get("staffSession");
    if (!session) throw new Error("a staff route ran without requireStaff");
    return session;
  };

  /** The confirmation requireStaffStepUp verified; a route without it in front is a wiring fault, not a refusal. */
  const confirmedStepUp = (c: Context<AppEnv>): StaffStepUpConfirmed => {
    const confirmed = c.get("staffStepUp");
    if (!confirmed) throw new Error("a staff route that changes something ran without requireStaffStepUp");
    return confirmed;
  };

  // A decision on a case: the path's case is the action's target, and the body is the action's params with the assertion
  // as `stepUp`. The decision commits with its audit row or not at all. When the confirming key or account no longer
  // opens anything by then, the session that confirmed has ended, and requireStaff clears both cookies on that answer as
  // on its own; when the challenge's time ran out, the console asks for the key again.
  routes.post(
    "/cases/:case/decisions",
    auth.requireStaff,
    auth.requireStaffStepUp("case_decided", (c) => c.req.param("case")),
    async (c) => {
      const outcome = await moderation.decide(staffSession(c), confirmedStepUp(c), { requestId: c.get("requestId") });
      if (outcome === "ended") throw new AuthError("staff_session_required", 401);
      if (outcome === "late") throw new AuthError("challenge_expired", 400);
      const answer: CaseDecisionResponse = { decisionId: outcome.decisionId };
      return c.json(answer, 201);
    },
  );

  return routes;
}
```

### Create `packages/db/migrations/0016_decisions_and_ledger.sql`

```sql
-- Decisions and the ledger (3c design, section 6.2). Written by hand: this migration changes no table. The API inserts a
-- decision and its measures; the triggers below check them, force what the API must not choose, and derive every post's
-- level and every image's state from the ledger of measures (decision_actions, with seal_posts), so that no restriction
-- exists without a decision a staff key confirmed. Every function is owned by the migrator, pins its search path, names
-- every object schema-qualified and has EXECUTE taken from PUBLIC: a trigger function fires for every role all the same,
-- and the few that a role calls directly are granted to that role alone. Errors carry their code as the message under
-- SQLSTATE P0001 unless a SQLSTATE is named. Under READ COMMITTED each statement of a PL/pgSQL function takes a fresh
-- snapshot, so a read in a statement of its own after a lock sees every row committed while the lock waited: the
-- functions below are written in that form wherever a lock comes first.
--
-- Whether an account is staff, for the rule that no final measure restricts a staff account. It runs as its owner, since
-- the API role holds nothing in the auth schema, and it takes the account's row FOR SHARE: a concurrent promotion either
-- waits for the decision's commit or is read by it (FOR KEY SHARE would let a promotion slip between the read and the
-- commit). False when there is no such account. Only the triggers below call it.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."account_is_staff"(account uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = auth, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  staff boolean;
BEGIN
  SELECT u.role <> 'user' INTO staff FROM auth.users u WHERE u.id = account_is_staff.account FOR SHARE;
  RETURN coalesce(staff, false);
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."account_is_staff"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Recusal: whether a staff account is too close to the parties of a case to decide it. True when the staff account is
-- itself a party, or a personal account the operator linked to it (auth.staff_personal_accounts, which no API role can
-- read) is a party, follows, blocks or mutes one, replied to a post of one in the last 90 days, or wrote the post that the
-- case's own post replies to or quotes. Only what the linked account did, and the post the case judges, count: a party's
-- own follow, block, mute or reply towards a linked account never does, since anyone can make one without the staff member
-- doing anything, and one click would otherwise put an account beyond every staff member whose posting account it follows.
-- It runs as its owner and answers one boolean. Only the triggers below and staff_case_conflict call it.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."staff_party_conflict"(staff uuid, parties uuid[], target_post uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT coalesce(staff_party_conflict.staff = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties), false)
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM auth.staff_personal_accounts l
       WHERE l.staff_user_id = staff_party_conflict.staff
         AND (l.personal_user_id = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties)
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.follows f WHERE f.follower_id = l.personal_user_id AND f.followee_id = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties))
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.blocks b WHERE b.blocker_id = l.personal_user_id AND b.blocked_id = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties))
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.mutes m WHERE m.muter_id = l.personal_user_id AND m.muted_id = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties))
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.posts r JOIN public.posts o ON o.id = r.reply_to_id
                       WHERE r.author_id = l.personal_user_id AND o.author_id = ANY(staff_party_conflict.parties) AND r.created_at > now() - interval '90 days')
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.posts t JOIN public.posts o ON o.id IN (t.reply_to_id, t.quote_of_id)
                       WHERE t.id = staff_party_conflict.target_post AND o.author_id = l.personal_user_id)))
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."staff_party_conflict"(uuid, uuid[], uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
-- The same question about a case, for the routes: they hand over a case, never a list of accounts. False when the case
-- does not exist. The parties are the case's subject (a post's author, or the account) and, with `everyone`, every
-- signed-in reporter of its items; without it a refused read says nothing about who reported.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."staff_case_conflict"(staff uuid, case_id uuid, everyone boolean) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  c public.cases;
  subject uuid;
  parties uuid[];
BEGIN
  SELECT k.* INTO c FROM public.cases k WHERE k.id = staff_case_conflict.case_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RETURN false;
  END IF;
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    SELECT p.author_id INTO subject FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = c.target_id;
  ELSE
    subject := c.target_id;
  END IF;
  parties := array_remove(ARRAY[subject], NULL);
  IF staff_case_conflict.everyone THEN
    parties := parties || coalesce((SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT i.reporter_account_id) FROM public.intake_items i
                                     WHERE i.case_id = c.id AND i.reporter_account_id IS NOT NULL), '{}'::uuid[]);
  END IF;
  RETURN public.staff_party_conflict(staff_case_conflict.staff, parties, CASE WHEN c.target_type = 'post' THEN c.target_id END);
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."staff_case_conflict"(uuid, uuid, boolean) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."staff_case_conflict"(uuid, uuid, boolean) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- The one predicate by which a snapshot's content is withheld wherever it would be shown: true when the snapshot is
-- erased, or when it holds content (a body that is not empty, or an image with an alt text) and its post's content was
-- erased since (posts.erased_at). A snapshot taken after such an erasure holds no content, so it is shown as it is. An id
-- that names no snapshot is answered true: there is nothing to show.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."snapshot_withheld"(snapshot uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT coalesce((
    SELECT s.erased_at IS NOT NULL
        OR ((coalesce(s.body, '') <> ''
             OR CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(s.media) = 'array'
                     THEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(s.media) image WHERE image ->> 'alt' IS NOT NULL)
                     ELSE false END)
            AND s.target_type = 'post'
            AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = s.target_id AND p.erased_at IS NOT NULL))
      FROM public.evidence_snapshots s WHERE s.id = snapshot_withheld.snapshot), true)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."snapshot_withheld"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."snapshot_withheld"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- The one writer of the moderation columns: posts.moderation_level, posts.state other than the author's deletion, and
-- post_media.moderation_state. It derives them from the ledger: a post's level is the strongest post measure in force over
-- every case (removed also when its content was erased), and an image is sealed while a seal in force lists its post, else
-- removed, withheld or visible by the image measures in force (removed also when it was erased). The result does not
-- depend on the order in which cases, measures and reversals arrive, and an auditor can recompute it. With `levels` it
-- takes the posts first, in id order, then their image rows in id order; without it only the image rows, which is the form
-- a seal uses: a seal changes no post's level, images come onto a post only in the transaction that creates it, and an
-- image never leaves its post, so the image rows are where the derivation of image states serialises. Each read is a
-- statement of its own after its locks. posts.state mirrors the level unless the author deleted the post: the author's
-- deletion is terminal, and moderation never moves state to or from it. Nobody may call it: its owner does, from the
-- triggers below and from the erasure of a later migration.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."moderation_apply"(posts uuid[], levels boolean) RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  ids uuid[];
  derived public.moderation_level[];
BEGIN
  IF moderation_apply.levels THEN
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = ANY(moderation_apply.posts) ORDER BY p.id FOR UPDATE;
    SELECT array_agg(p.id),
           array_agg(CASE
             WHEN p.erased_at IS NOT NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.post_id = p.id AND m.kind = 'remove') THEN 'removed'
             WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.post_id = p.id AND m.kind = 'withhold') THEN 'withheld'
             ELSE 'visible' END::public.moderation_level)
      INTO ids, derived
      FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = ANY(moderation_apply.posts);
    UPDATE public.posts p SET moderation_level = v.level
      FROM unnest(ids, derived) AS v(id, level)
     WHERE p.id = v.id AND p.moderation_level <> v.level;
    UPDATE public.posts p SET state = v.level::text::public.post_state
      FROM unnest(ids, derived) AS v(id, level)
     WHERE p.id = v.id AND p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' AND p.state <> v.level::text::public.post_state;
  END IF;
  PERFORM 1 FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.post_id = ANY(moderation_apply.posts) ORDER BY m.id FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
  UPDATE public.post_media i SET moderation_state = v.state
    FROM (SELECT m.id,
                 CASE
                   WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.seal_posts s JOIN public.measures_in_force f ON f.id = s.action_id WHERE s.post_id = m.post_id) THEN 'sealed'
                   WHEN m.erased_at IS NOT NULL
                     OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force f WHERE f.post_id = m.post_id AND f.kind = 'remove_media' AND f.media_id = m.id) THEN 'removed'
                   WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force f WHERE f.post_id = m.post_id AND f.kind = 'withhold_media' AND f.media_id = m.id) THEN 'withheld'
                   ELSE 'visible' END::public.media_moderation_state AS state
            FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.post_id = ANY(moderation_apply.posts)) v
   WHERE i.id = v.id AND i.moderation_state <> v.state;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."moderation_apply"(uuid[], boolean) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
-- The posts' guard. The column grants of migration 0015 leave posts.state writable by the API role, which the author's
-- deletion needs; this trigger holds what it may write there. For every role, the migrator included: a post never leaves
-- deleted_by_author. For every role but the migrator: a post is inserted visible, at level visible and unerased, and an
-- update moves state only to deleted_by_author and never changes the level or the erasure time. The function is plain, so
-- current_user is the role that ran the statement: the API role can neither become the migrator nor switch the trigger
-- off, and inside the migrator-owned definer functions (moderation_apply, and the erasure of a later migration) it is the
-- migrator. The update trigger fires only for a statement that names one of the three columns and really changes one, so
-- the counter updates of likes, reposts, replies and quotes never meet it.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."posts_guard"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF current_user <> 'korbat_migrate' AND (NEW.state <> 'visible' OR NEW.moderation_level <> 'visible' OR NEW.erased_at IS NOT NULL) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.state = 'deleted_by_author' AND NEW.state <> 'deleted_by_author' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  IF current_user <> 'korbat_migrate' AND ((NEW.state IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.state AND NEW.state <> 'deleted_by_author')
      OR NEW.moderation_level IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.moderation_level OR NEW.erased_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.erased_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."posts_guard"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "posts_guard_insert" BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."posts" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."posts_guard"();--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "posts_guard_update" BEFORE UPDATE OF "state", "moderation_level", "erased_at" ON "public"."posts" FOR EACH ROW
  WHEN (OLD."state" IS DISTINCT FROM NEW."state" OR OLD."moderation_level" IS DISTINCT FROM NEW."moderation_level" OR OLD."erased_at" IS DISTINCT FROM NEW."erased_at")
  EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."posts_guard"();--> statement-breakpoint
-- A decision is checked and completed before it is stored. Whatever the insert supplied, the database sets when and in
-- which transaction it was decided, its public id, the first item it answers, its source, that nothing was automated and
-- that it applies everywhere, whether it rests on a suspect item, whether nobody could open the post's images when it was
-- taken, whether it needed an admin, whether it ended something done while deciding, and whether its author is told. It
-- runs as its owner (the API role cannot lock a case or read the auth schema). In this order:
--   1. The case, FOR UPDATE until the commit: two decisions of one case run one after the other, and no item attaches
--      meanwhile. The decision names the version of the case its moderator saw and is refused (case_changed) when another
--      decision landed since.
--   2. The kind and its outcomes. An interim decision restricts, on an open case. A final one restricts or finds no
--      breach, on an open case, and answers the items from the first unanswered one through through_seq, which must lie in
--      that range (case_changed otherwise: the items moved). A correction reverses, in part or in full, a restricting
--      interim or final decision of the same case, carries that decision's category and rules version and has a reason. A
--      review is refused until the migration that brings appeals replaces this function. Anything else is invalid_decision.
--   3. The snapshot belongs to the case, is not erased and has the digest the decision names.
--   4. Each text the decision names by its digest is a saved, unconfirmed, unerased text of this case by the deciding
--      account, of the matching kind.
--   5. The parties: the case's subject and the signed-in reporters of the items the decision considers. A deciding account
--      that is one of them, or close to one through a linked personal account, is refused (staff_recused).
--   6. The role and the suspicion. The deciding account's row and then the subject's are taken FOR SHARE, so a demotion or
--      a promotion either waits for the commit or is read here. suspect, unseen and needs_admin are forced. A final
--      decision that answers a suspect item answers every unanswered suspect item of its case (case_changed when one lies
--      beyond its range), so none is left behind and a seal taken while deciding never ends while one is unanswered. A
--      decision under R2 rests on a suspect item. Only an admin takes a decision that needs one (admin_required); an
--      interim decision never does, so whoever is on duty can seal reported images or withhold a threat at once.
--   7. The caps, under an advisory lock of the deciding account held until the commit, so one person's decisions are
--      counted one at a time: no more decisions in the last hour or day than moderation_limits allows (decision_cap).
--   8. The ground: "illegal", and the outcome "illegality not evident", each need a considered item that alleges
--      illegality.
--   9. The source, from the considered items: a notice, a report, or the moderator's own finding.
--  10. Telling. A final decision that closes its case while a measure taken while deciding, of which the author was told,
--      is in force ends that measure, and says so. The author is told of an interim decision (unless the target is
--      deleted, since such a measure can never take effect), of a final restriction, of a correction of a decision they
--      were told of, and of every decision that ends something they were told of; of nothing else.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."decisions_record"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  c public.cases;
  corrected public.decisions;
  snapshot public.evidence_snapshots;
  subject uuid;
  reporters uuid[];
  considers_suspect boolean;
  considers_illegal boolean;
  considers_r5 boolean;
  from_notice boolean;
  from_user boolean;
  decider_role text;
  frozen boolean;
  per_hour integer;
  per_day integer;
  in_hour integer;
  in_day integer;
  reason_kind public.staff_text_kind;
  ends_interim boolean := false;
  target_deleted boolean;
BEGIN
  NEW.decided_at := now();
  NEW.xact := pg_current_xact_id();
  NEW.puid := replace(gen_random_uuid()::text, '-', '');
  NEW.informed_at := NEW.decided_at;
  NEW.answers_from_seq := NULL;
  NEW.automated_detection := false;
  NEW.automated_decision := 'not_automated';
  NEW.territorial_scope := 'worldwide';
  NEW.author_mail_at := NULL;
  -- Only the erasure of a later migration marks a decision redacted.
  NEW.redacted_at := NULL;

  -- 1.
  SELECT k.* INTO c FROM public.cases k WHERE k.id = NEW.case_id FOR UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'a decision names a case that does not exist' USING ERRCODE = '23503';
  END IF;
  IF c.state_version IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.seen_state_version THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'case_changed';
  END IF;

  -- 2.
  IF NEW.kind = 'interim' THEN
    IF NEW.outcome <> 'restricted' OR c.closed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'An interim decision restricts, on an open case.';
    END IF;
  ELSIF NEW.kind = 'final' THEN
    IF NEW.outcome NOT IN ('restricted', 'no_violation', 'not_evident') OR c.closed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'A final decision restricts or finds no breach, on an open case.';
    END IF;
    IF NOT (c.answered_seq < NEW.through_seq AND NEW.through_seq <= c.intake_seq) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'case_changed';
    END IF;
    NEW.answers_from_seq := c.answered_seq + 1;
  ELSIF NEW.kind = 'correction' THEN
    SELECT d.* INTO corrected FROM public.decisions d
     WHERE d.id = NEW.reviews_decision_id AND d.case_id = NEW.case_id AND d.kind IN ('interim', 'final') AND d.outcome = 'restricted';
    IF NOT FOUND OR NEW.outcome NOT IN ('partly_reversed', 'reversed') OR NEW.category <> corrected.category
       OR NEW.rules_version <> corrected.rules_version OR NEW.reason_digest IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'A correction reverses a restricting decision of its case, with that decision''s category and rules version and a reason.';
    END IF;
  ELSE
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'A review waits for the migration that brings appeals.';
  END IF;

  -- 3.
  SELECT s.* INTO snapshot FROM public.evidence_snapshots s WHERE s.id = NEW.snapshot_id;
  IF NOT FOUND OR snapshot.case_id <> NEW.case_id THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'snapshot_mismatch';
  END IF;
  IF snapshot.erased_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'snapshot_erased';
  END IF;
  IF snapshot.digest IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.snapshot_digest THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'snapshot_mismatch';
  END IF;

  -- 4. A read: decisions_apply confirms the texts, and refuses when one is gone by then.
  reason_kind := CASE WHEN NEW.kind IN ('review', 'correction') THEN 'review_reason' ELSE 'reason' END;
  IF (NEW.facts_digest IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM public.staff_texts t WHERE t.digest = NEW.facts_digest AND t.case_id = NEW.case_id AND t.author_id = NEW.decided_by
           AND t.kind = 'facts' AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL))
     OR (NEW.reason_digest IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM public.staff_texts t WHERE t.digest = NEW.reason_digest AND t.case_id = NEW.case_id AND t.author_id = NEW.decided_by
           AND t.kind = reason_kind AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL))
     OR (NEW.legal_reference_digest IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM public.staff_texts t WHERE t.digest = NEW.legal_reference_digest AND t.case_id = NEW.case_id AND t.author_id = NEW.decided_by
           AND t.kind = 'legal_reference' AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL)) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'text_not_found';
  END IF;

  -- 5. What the decision considers: a final decision the items it answers, an interim one every unanswered item, a
  -- correction the items its corrected decision answered (for a corrected interim decision, every unanswered item). One
  -- statement after the case's lock reads every fact the steps below need of them.
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    SELECT p.author_id INTO subject FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = c.target_id;
  ELSE
    subject := c.target_id;
  END IF;
  SELECT coalesce(array_agg(DISTINCT i.reporter_account_id) FILTER (WHERE i.reporter_account_id IS NOT NULL), '{}'::uuid[]),
         coalesce(bool_or(i.suspect), false),
         coalesce(bool_or(i.alleges_illegal), false),
         coalesce(bool_or(n.rule_id = 'R5'), false),
         coalesce(bool_or(n.kind = 'user' AND i.alleges_illegal), false),
         coalesce(bool_or(n.kind = 'user'), false)
    INTO reporters, considers_suspect, considers_illegal, considers_r5, from_notice, from_user
    FROM public.intake_items i JOIN public.intakes n ON n.id = i.intake_id
   WHERE i.case_id = NEW.case_id
     AND CASE WHEN NEW.kind = 'final' THEN i.seq BETWEEN NEW.answers_from_seq AND NEW.through_seq
              WHEN NEW.kind = 'correction' AND corrected.kind = 'final' THEN i.answered_by = corrected.id
              ELSE i.answered_by IS NULL END;
  IF public.staff_party_conflict(NEW.decided_by, array_remove(ARRAY[subject], NULL) || reporters, CASE WHEN c.target_type = 'post' THEN c.target_id END) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_recused';
  END IF;

  -- 6.
  SELECT u.role::text INTO decider_role FROM auth.users u WHERE u.id = NEW.decided_by FOR SHARE;
  PERFORM public.account_is_staff(subject);
  NEW.suspect := CASE WHEN NEW.kind = 'correction' THEN corrected.suspect ELSE considers_suspect END;
  NEW.unseen := false;
  IF NEW.kind = 'final' AND c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    -- Read now, before decisions_apply answers anything: frozen through a suspect item of this case, through the author's
    -- account's case, or through a seal in force.
    SELECT public.post_frozen(c.target_id) INTO frozen;
    NEW.unseen := coalesce(frozen, false);
  END IF;
  IF NEW.kind = 'final' AND NEW.suspect AND EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM public.intake_items i WHERE i.case_id = NEW.case_id AND i.suspect AND i.answered_by IS NULL AND i.seq > NEW.through_seq) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'case_changed';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.rule_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM 'R2' AND NOT NEW.suspect THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'A decision under R2 rests on a suspect item: a finding citing R2 is opened first.';
  END IF;
  NEW.needs_admin := CASE NEW.kind
                       WHEN 'final' THEN NEW.suspect OR considers_r5 OR coalesce(NEW.rule_id IN ('R2', 'R5'), false)
                       WHEN 'correction' THEN corrected.needs_admin
                       ELSE false END;
  IF NEW.needs_admin AND decider_role IS DISTINCT FROM 'admin' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'admin_required';
  END IF;

  -- 7. A one-bigint key: the social module's pair locks use the two-key space, so the two never meet.
  PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('korbat.decision_cap:' || NEW.decided_by::text, 0));
  SELECT l.decisions_per_hour, l.decisions_per_day INTO per_hour, per_day FROM public.moderation_limits l WHERE l.id = 1;
  SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE d.decided_at > now() - interval '1 hour'), count(*) INTO in_hour, in_day
    FROM public.decisions d WHERE d.decided_by = NEW.decided_by AND d.decided_at > now() - interval '1 day';
  IF in_hour >= coalesce(per_hour, 60) OR in_day >= coalesce(per_day, 300) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'decision_cap';
  END IF;

  -- 8.
  IF (NEW.ground IS NOT DISTINCT FROM 'illegal' OR NEW.outcome = 'not_evident') AND NOT considers_illegal THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision' USING DETAIL = 'The ground of the law, and "illegality not evident", need a considered item that alleges illegality.';
  END IF;

  -- 9.
  NEW.source := CASE WHEN NEW.kind = 'correction' THEN corrected.source
                     WHEN from_notice THEN 'notice'::public.decision_source
                     WHEN from_user THEN 'report'::public.decision_source
                     ELSE 'own_initiative'::public.decision_source END;

  -- 10. Both reads come after the case's lock and after the subject's profile lock, which the deciding transaction takes
  -- first and the author's deletion and the purge take too, so the target cannot be deleted before the commit.
  IF NEW.kind = 'final' AND NEW.through_seq = c.intake_seq THEN
    SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = m.decision_id
                    WHERE m.case_id = NEW.case_id AND m.decision_kind = 'interim' AND m.kind <> 'seal_media' AND d.author_mail <> 'none')
      INTO ends_interim;
  END IF;
  NEW.ended_interim := ends_interim;
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    SELECT p.state = 'deleted_by_author' INTO target_deleted FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = c.target_id;
  ELSE
    SELECT p.deleted_at IS NOT NULL INTO target_deleted FROM public.profiles p WHERE p.id = c.target_id;
  END IF;
  NEW.author_mail := CASE
                       WHEN NEW.ended_interim THEN 'pending'
                       WHEN NEW.kind = 'interim' AND NOT coalesce(target_deleted, false) THEN 'pending'
                       WHEN NEW.kind = 'final' AND NEW.outcome = 'restricted' THEN 'pending'
                       WHEN NEW.kind = 'correction' AND corrected.author_mail <> 'none' THEN 'pending'
                       ELSE 'none' END::public.delivery_state;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."decisions_record"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "decisions_record" BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."decisions" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."decisions_record"();--> statement-breakpoint
-- What a stored decision does to its case, before any of its measures exists (they are inserted after it, and their own
-- triggers do the rest). A final decision answers its items: a restriction on the law as restricted_legal, on a rule as
-- restricted_rule; "illegality not evident" as that on an item that alleged illegality and as no_violation on any other;
-- "no breach" as no_violation. Every decision moves the case's version. A final one moves answered_seq, recomputes the
-- lane and the oldest open time from the items still unanswered, closes the case when none is left, and for a post case
-- it closed derives the post's level again, so that what was done while deciding ends. One place decides that a seal taken
-- while deciding has ended: this trigger reads the case's such seals in force before it answers the items and again
-- after, derives the image states of every post an ended seal listed, and, when the author was told of one of them, marks
-- the decision as ending it and tells them. Last, it confirms the decision's texts, and refuses (text_not_found) unless it
-- confirmed one text for each digest the decision names: a sweep that deleted a text since decisions_record read it would
-- otherwise leave the decision naming nothing.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."decisions_apply"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  c public.cases;
  seals_before uuid[];
  ended uuid[];
  listed uuid[];
  open_items integer;
  open_lane smallint;
  oldest timestamptz;
  digests text[];
  confirmed integer;
BEGIN
  IF NEW.kind = 'final' THEN
    SELECT coalesce(array_agg(m.id), '{}'::uuid[]) INTO seals_before
      FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.case_id = NEW.case_id AND m.kind = 'seal_media' AND m.decision_kind = 'interim';
    UPDATE public.intake_items i
       SET answered_by = NEW.id,
           outcome = CASE NEW.outcome
                       WHEN 'restricted' THEN CASE WHEN NEW.ground = 'illegal' THEN 'restricted_legal' ELSE 'restricted_rule' END
                       WHEN 'not_evident' THEN CASE WHEN i.alleges_illegal THEN 'not_evident' ELSE 'no_violation' END
                       ELSE 'no_violation' END::public.item_outcome
     WHERE i.case_id = NEW.case_id AND i.seq BETWEEN NEW.answers_from_seq AND NEW.through_seq AND i.answered_by IS NULL;
    SELECT count(*), min(i.lane), min(i.created_at) INTO open_items, open_lane, oldest
      FROM public.intake_items i WHERE i.case_id = NEW.case_id AND i.answered_by IS NULL;
    UPDATE public.cases k
       SET state_version = k.state_version + 1,
           last_decided_at = now(),
           answered_seq = NEW.through_seq,
           lane = coalesce(open_lane, 2),
           oldest_open_at = oldest,
           closed_at = CASE WHEN open_items = 0 THEN now() END
     WHERE k.id = NEW.case_id
    RETURNING k.* INTO c;
    IF c.closed_at IS NOT NULL AND c.target_type = 'post' THEN
      PERFORM public.moderation_apply(ARRAY[c.target_id], true);
    END IF;
    SELECT coalesce(array_agg(s.id), '{}'::uuid[]) INTO ended
      FROM unnest(seals_before) AS s(id) WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.id = s.id);
    IF cardinality(ended) > 0 THEN
      SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT s.post_id) INTO listed FROM public.seal_posts s WHERE s.action_id = ANY(ended);
      PERFORM public.moderation_apply(listed, false);
      IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.decision_actions a JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = a.decision_id WHERE a.id = ANY(ended) AND d.author_mail <> 'none') THEN
        UPDATE public.decisions d
           SET ended_interim = true, author_mail = CASE WHEN d.author_mail = 'none' THEN 'pending'::public.delivery_state ELSE d.author_mail END
         WHERE d.id = NEW.id;
      END IF;
    END IF;
  ELSE
    UPDATE public.cases k SET state_version = k.state_version + 1, last_decided_at = now() WHERE k.id = NEW.case_id;
  END IF;

  digests := array_remove(ARRAY[NEW.facts_digest, NEW.reason_digest, NEW.legal_reference_digest], NULL);
  IF cardinality(digests) > 0 THEN
    UPDATE public.staff_texts t SET decision_id = NEW.id, confirmed_at = now()
     WHERE t.digest = ANY(digests) AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL;
    GET DIAGNOSTICS confirmed = ROW_COUNT;
    IF confirmed <> cardinality(digests) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'text_not_found';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."decisions_apply"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "decisions_apply" AFTER INSERT ON "public"."decisions" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."decisions_apply"();--> statement-breakpoint
-- A measure or a reversal is checked and completed before it joins the ledger. In this order:
--   1. Its decision was inserted by this transaction: the stored transaction id and the decision's time are compared
--      together, a pair a logical restore cannot reproduce (it restarts the counter while rows keep their stamps). So a
--      row is added to the ledger only with its own confirmed decision.
--   2. The columns the API must not choose are cleared and forced: the subject, the post, the measure a reversal lifts,
--      whether the measure changed anything, and the time; a seal and its lifting name no image.
--   3. Fit. Post and image kinds only on a post case, field kinds only on an account case. An interim decision withholds
--      (the post or one image) or resets a field; a final one removes or resets; either may seal the images its case
--      reaches, and either may lift the case's interim withhold of the post or of an image. A correction or a review holds
--      reversals only, and only one of them lifts a seal. A decision holds at most one post measure. An image measure
--      names an image of the post; no other kind names one.
--   4. On a post case the post is locked FOR UPDATE, the lock moderation_apply takes after the insert, taken earlier in
--      the same order; what follows is read in statements of their own.
--   5. A second interim withhold of the post, or of the same image, while one is in force in the case is refused. A second
--      interim reset is not: its author may set the field again at any time, so whoever is on duty can reset it again.
--   6. A reversal names exactly one measure: for a correction or a review the measure of the matching kind and image held
--      by the reviewed decision; for an interim or final decision the case's interim withhold of that kind and image in
--      force. That measure must be in force. There is never a choice among several, and no search for "the newest".
--   7. A seal needs a decision that rests on a suspect item and is under R2 or in the category Protection of minors. It
--      is not refused because a seal of the case is already in force: each seal has its own list, which on an account's
--      case is how images posted since are covered.
--   8. No measure of a decision that is not interim restricts a staff account (staff_target): staff are disciplined by
--      demotion, while an interim measure applies to them as to anyone.
--   9. Lifting a seal needs an admin, whatever the decision's kind, and marks the decision as needing one.
--  10. Whether the measure changes anything now: "deleted" when the post or the account is deleted; "already" when the
--      post's level already is at least the measure's, when an image's post is not visible or the image's own state already
--      is at least the measure's, or when the field already holds its placeholder; else null. A seal's is set by
--      decision_actions_apply, once it has made the seal's list.
--  11. A reversal of an interim measure of which the author was told marks the decision as ending it and tells them.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."decision_actions_check"() RETURNS trigger
```
